questions.question: Who is Alyx's father, a former Black Mesa scientist and the leader of the human resistance?

questions.explanation: Known simply as 'Alyx's Gun' in the game files and community, this unique firearm is a heavily modified machine pistol that is her signature weapon.
questions.question: What is the name of Alyx's custom-made, fully automatic pistol that she uses throughout the game?

questions.explanation: Alyx guides Gordon through the rooftops and back alleys of City 17 to the hidden lab of Dr. Kleiner, one of the few surviving scientists from Black Mesa.
questions.question: Early in the game, Alyx saves Gordon from Civil Protection officers and leads him to whose secret laboratory?

questions.explanation: The Citadel is the central command hub for the Combine on Earth, housing the offices of Dr. Breen and the technology that suppresses humanity.
questions.question: What is the name of the imposing Combine fortress that looms over City 17?

questions.explanation: Her custom-built EMP Tool can retract force fields, open locked doors, and even reprogram Combine roller mines to fight for the resistance.
questions.question: What is the name of the multi-purpose electronic tool Alyx uses to bypass Combine security systems?

questions.explanation: Dr. Mossman's loyalty is often in question, creating tension with Alyx, though she ultimately proves to be an ally to the resistance.
questions.question: Which former Black Mesa scientist, who has a complicated relationship with Eli, works alongside the resistance at Black Mesa East?

questions.explanation: Alyx can re-purpose the Combine's own automated turrets, turning them against their former masters to cover Gordon's advance.
questions.question: In the depths of Nova Prospekt, Alyx demonstrates her hacking skills by reprogramming what type of Combine automated defense system?

questions.explanation: Their successful attack on the prison served as the catalyst for the citizens of City 17 to finally rise up in open rebellion against the Combine.
questions.question: After escaping Nova Prospekt, Gordon and Alyx are teleported one week into the future, an event that sparks what city-wide uprising?

questions.explanation: By retrieving 'Pheropods' from an Antlion Guard, Alyx allows Gordon to command the subterranean creatures, turning them into powerful allies on the coast.
questions.question: What insectoid alien species, native to Xen, does Alyx help Gordon pacify and command using Pheropods?

questions.explanation: The Citadel's primary energy core becomes unstable after Gordon destroys the main reactor, forcing them on a perilous journey back inside to contain it.
questions.question: In Episode One, what specific structure within the Citadel must Alyx and Gordon stabilize to delay its explosion?

questions.explanation: The G-Man shows Gordon a vision of him carrying a young Alyx out of the Black Mesa dormitories, saving her from the destruction she otherwise would not have survived.
questions.question: In Episode Two, the G-Man reveals he rescued a young Alyx from what catastrophic event?

questions.explanation: The White Forest base is the last major resistance stronghold, housing the rocket they plan to use to shut down the Combine's superportal.
questions.question: What is the name of the resistance base located in an old missile silo, which serves as the main setting for Episode Two?

questions.explanation: Dr. Arne Magnusson is a pompous but brilliant scientist from the Black Mesa days who constantly belittles Gordon while preparing the crucial satellite launch.
questions.question: What is the first name of the smug, rocket-obsessed scientist Alyx and Gordon work with at White Forest?

meta.lore_desc: A key figure in the human resistance against the Combine. She is a skilled hacker, brilliant engineer, and a close companion to Gordon Freeman.

questions.explanation: The G-Man is rarely seen without his standard-issue briefcase, the contents of which remain one of the series' greatest mysteries.
questions.question: What is the G-Man's signature accessory, which he is almost never seen without?

questions.explanation: His clean, simple blue business suit and tie contribute to his unsettlingly mundane appearance, which contrasts with his extraordinary powers.
questions.question: What is the G-Man's typical attire, giving him the appearance of a government agent or corporate bureaucrat?

questions.explanation: Gordon's consciousness awakens to the G-Man's face on a ghostly train, a surreal callback to the train ride that began the original Half-Life.
questions.question: At the start of Half-Life 2, the G-Man delivers his cryptic monologue to Gordon aboard what type of vehicle?

questions.explanation: 'The right man in the wrong place can make all the difference in the world' is one of the G-Man's most iconic lines, summarizing his use of Gordon as a catalyst.
questions.question: The G-Man often refers to Gordon Freeman as 'the right man in the wrong...' what?

questions.explanation: The G-Man frequently makes a small, precise motion to adjust his tie, a tic that adds to his strange and unsettling demeanor.
questions.question: What is the G-Man's most notable physical characteristic, often seen when he is speaking?

questions.explanation: Just as he did at the end of the first game, the G-Man attempts to place Gordon back into stasis, referring to it as 'a choice' Gordon does not get to make.
questions.question: At the end of Half-Life 2, the G-Man freezes time and puts Gordon into what state before the Vortigaunts intervene?

questions.explanation: This chilling line immediately sets the bleak, post-apocalyptic tone of the world Gordon is about to re-enter after his long stasis.
questions.question: In his opening monologue of Half-Life 2, the G-Man tells Gordon to 'wake up and smell the...' what?

questions.explanation: He frequently mentions his 'employers' and their interest in Gordon's progress, but their true identity and motives are completely unknown.
questions.question: The G-Man claims to be working on behalf of what mysterious group?

questions.explanation: During the final confrontation, a monitor shows Dr. Breen speaking with the G-Man, who hints that Breen's 'contract was open to the highest bidder'.
questions.question: In Dr. Breen's office, who does the G-Man appear to be communicating with on a monitor, suggesting a prior deal was made?

questions.explanation: In a surprising show of power, a group of Vortigaunts surrounds the G-Man, blocking his influence and teleporting Gordon to safety, much to the G-Man's annoyance.
questions.question: In Episode One, which alien race directly intervenes to free Gordon from the G-Man's control?

questions.explanation: He implants this ominous message into Alyx's subconscious for her to repeat to her father, which causes Eli great distress and reveals his own past dealings with the G-Man.
questions.question: In Episode Two, the G-Man instructs Gordon to deliver a specific five-word message to Eli Vance. What is that message?
wrong: The resonance cascade was a lie

questions.explanation: A shaken Eli Vance reveals to Gordon that the G-Man whispered the 'unforeseen consequences' warning to him just before the experiment, and delivered the crystal himself.
questions.question: According to Eli Vance, who provided the specific crystal sample that caused the resonance cascade at Black Mesa?

questions.correct: A chance to save her father
questions.explanation: The G-Man offers Alyx the chance to avert her father's death at the hands of a Combine Advisor, an offer she accepts, thus placing her in his employment.
questions.question: At the end of Half-Life: Alyx, the G-Man offers Alyx a reward for her help. What does he offer?

questions.explanation: He states that his previous hire, Gordon Freeman, has been 'unable or unwilling' to perform his tasks, and that Alyx is a worthy replacement.
questions.question: After Alyx accepts his offer, the G-Man refers to her as a suitable 'replacement' for whom?

questions.explanation: His tendency to stress the wrong parts of words, like 'sy-LA-ble' instead of 'SYL-la-ble', contributes to his alien and unsettling presence.
questions.question: The G-Man's strange speech patterns include mispronunciations, odd pauses, and putting emphasis on the wrong what?

meta.lore_desc: A mysterious and powerful interdimensional being. He appears to manipulate events from behind the scenes for his unseen 'employers,' with Gordon Freeman as his primary pawn.

questions.explanation: The bright red paint job with worn, metallic edges makes the crowbar instantly recognizable, even at a glance.
questions.question: What is the distinctive color of the crowbar wielded by Gordon Freeman?

questions.explanation: Scattered throughout the world are Lambda-marked supply crates, which can only be opened with a good whack from the crowbar to reveal health and ammo.
questions.question: Besides being a weapon, the crowbar is most frequently used to break open what kind of item?

questions.explanation: Barney, the former Black Mesa security guard now working undercover in Civil Protection, reunites Gordon with his favorite tool in Dr. Kleiner's lab.
questions.question: In Half-Life 2, which character famously returns the crowbar to Gordon, saying 'I think you dropped this back at Black Mesa'?

questions.explanation: A single, well-timed swing from the crowbar is all it takes to dispatch a standard headcrab, making it an essential tool for conservation of ammo.
questions.question: The crowbar is the perfect tool for dealing with which small, head-hugging alien parasite?

questions.explanation: The Lambda symbol, representing the lab where the resonance cascade began, was adopted by the resistance as their logo, signifying hope and rebellion.
questions.question: The crowbar is a symbol of the resistance, often seen in graffiti alongside what Greek letter?

questions.explanation: While trying to help, Gordon pushes a plug into a socket with the crowbar, causing a power surge that sends him teleporting all over City 17.
questions.question: In Dr. Kleiner's lab, Gordon accidentally breaks what object with the crowbar, causing the teleport to malfunction?

questions.explanation: Ravenholm is a horror-themed level filled with zombies and headcrabs, forcing the player to rely heavily on the crowbar and environmental traps to survive.
questions.question: What zombie-infested mining town is notorious for the phrase 'We don't go there anymore,' a place where the crowbar is indispensable?

questions.explanation: He finds it on the floor of a storage area in Sector C, using it to break the glass on a door control panel to escape a locked-down area.
questions.question: In the original Half-Life, Gordon picks up the crowbar for the first time in what kind of location?

questions.explanation: For the first part of the game, Gordon is completely unarmed, relying on the 'Use' key to open doors and interact with buttons.
questions.question: Before receiving the crowbar, what is the only way for Gordon to interact with the world in Half-Life 2?

questions.explanation: Gordon must use concrete blocks to weigh down one end of a see-saw, then break the wooden supports to create a ramp he can run up.
questions.question: In the chapter 'Route Kanal', the crowbar is essential for breaking wooden beams that are part of what type of physics puzzle?

questions.explanation: The popular co-op mod gives the crowbar a unique secondary function, allowing players to throw it like a spear, though they must then retrieve it.
questions.question: In the Half-Life 2 mod 'Synergy,' what does the crowbar's secondary fire do?

questions.explanation: Just as Gordon is about to teleport, Barney can be seen on the security monitor using his own crowbar to barricade a door against attackers.
questions.question: Which character uses a crowbar to help hold a door shut against Combine soldiers, right before Gordon enters the teleporter at Kleiner's lab?

questions.explanation: Once the Gravity Gun is supercharged in the Citadel, it can punt enemies with lethal force, making it a far more effective close-quarters weapon than the crowbar.
questions.question: The crowbar is made obsolete as a primary melee weapon by which later, more powerful device?

questions.explanation: Though not clearly visible in the final game, texture files reveal the brand 'Collins Dynamics Industrial,' a fictional company, on the side of the crowbar model.
questions.question: What is the real-world tool manufacturer whose logo is often found on the crowbar's texture files in early versions and fan-made models?

questions.explanation: Early beta versions of the game included a faster, weaker secondary fire for the crowbar that was a straightforward jab, which was removed for the final release.
questions.question: In the Half-Life 2 leak, the crowbar had a secondary attack that was cut from the final game. What was this attack?

meta.lore_desc: A simple steel prying tool, painted red. It is the signature melee weapon of Gordon Freeman and has become an iconic symbol of the human resistance.

questions.explanation: Dr. Eli Vance mentions its full name, though Alyx quickly shortens it to 'The G-Gun' for convenience.
questions.question: What is the official, scientific designation for the device commonly known as the 'Gravity Gun'?

questions.explanation: Alyx introduces the Gravity Gun by having Gordon play fetch with her robotic pet, Dog.
questions.question: In her lab at Black Mesa East, which character first gives Gordon Freeman the Gravity Gun and teaches him how to use it?

questions.explanation: Hopper Mines are a constant nuisance along the coastal chapters, but they become a powerful weapon when turned against their Combine masters.
questions.question: What common, three-legged explosive mine can be plucked from the ground and launched at enemies using the Gravity Gun?

questions.explanation: The secondary fire is key to the gun's utility, allowing the user to grab items from a distance before launching them with primary fire.
questions.question: The Gravity Gun's primary fire pushes objects away with a forceful blast. What does its secondary fire do?

questions.explanation: The iconic orange glow of the Gravity Gun matches the color scheme of Gordon Freeman's HEV Suit.
questions.question: The standard version of the Gravity Gun, before it is supercharged, emits an energy field of what distinct color from its 'prongs'?

questions.explanation: This 'blue' Gravity Gun, also called the Dark Energy Field Manipulator, is powerful enough to manipulate organic matter and vaporize soldiers.
questions.question: After passing through a Combine confiscation field in Nova Prospekt, the Gravity Gun becomes supercharged. What color does its energy field turn?

questions.explanation: Alyx's casual nickname for the device is much easier to say than its full, scientific designation.
questions.question: What is the nickname Alyx Vance affectionately uses for the Zero Point Energy Field Manipulator?

questions.explanation: These dark energy orbs are fired from wall-mounted emitters and are the primary ammunition for the Pulse Rifle's secondary fire.
questions.question: The supercharged Gravity Gun is the only weapon capable of catching and firing back what projectile, commonly used by Combine soldiers in the Citadel?

questions.explanation: While you can bat away a Gunship's energy projectiles, the gun itself cannot harm the heavily armored synth; only rockets will do the trick.
questions.question: The standard Gravity Gun is almost completely ineffective against which flying Combine synth, only able to deflect its main weapon?

questions.explanation: Eli Vance built Dog to protect Alyx. Despite his immense strength and intimidating appearance, he is exceptionally loyal and playful.
questions.question: At Black Mesa East, Alyx's massive robotic companion demonstrates the power of the Gravity Gun by tossing a car around. What is this robot's name?

questions.explanation: A direct hit from a Pulse Rifle energy ball is required to destroy a Strider's core, but the Gravity Gun is needed to expose it first.
questions.question: The supercharged Gravity Gun is the most effective tool for destroying which massive, three-legged Combine ground synth by ripping off its armor panels?

questions.explanation: Regular soldiers are immediately disintegrated by the blue Gravity Gun's field, but the heavily armored Elites can be briefly held before being launched.
questions.question: While the supercharged Gravity Gun can vaporize most Combine soldiers, what is the only type of soldier it can physically pick up and throw?

questions.explanation: These pods travel on energy rails and act as both elevators and barriers, requiring Gordon to use the gun to clear a path.
questions.question: During the final ascent of the Citadel, the supercharged Gravity Gun is essential for navigating past what hazardous form of Combine transportation?

questions.explanation: Eli remarks that he should have just given the Gravity Gun to Dog, as it would have saved everyone a lot of trouble.
questions.question: According to a conversation with Eli Vance, the Gravity Gun was originally built for heavy lifting and wasn't intended as a weapon. Who was its intended user?

questions.explanation: Normally a persistent nuisance, the Rollermine becomes one of the most powerful projectiles in the game when wielded by the blue Gravity Gun.
questions.question: What electrified, spherical enemy, when caught and launched by the supercharged Gravity Gun, is capable of vaporizing an entire squad of soldiers?

meta.lore_desc: Officially the Zero Point Energy Field Manipulator, this device projects a localized energy field, allowing the user to manipulate objects from a distance. A truly revolutionary tool for both industrial and defensive applications.

questions.explanation: The bright orange color makes the HEV suit one of the most recognizable outfits in video game history.
questions.question: What is the primary, iconic color of the plating on Gordon Freeman's HEV Suit?

questions.explanation: The health counter is a constant reminder of Gordon's mortality, ticking down with every hit he takes.
questions.question: On the suit's Heads-Up Display, what vital statistic is represented by a number next to a red cross symbol?

questions.explanation: The suit was designed for scientists at Black Mesa to work safely in labs with radiation, chemical spills, and other dangers.
questions.question: What does the 'HEV' in HEV Suit stand for?

questions.explanation: The suit's flashlight is essential for navigating dark tunnels and abandoned buildings, but it draws from the same auxiliary power as the sprint function.
questions.question: What built-in feature of the HEV suit allows Gordon to see in pitch-black areas?

questions.explanation: This symbol is located next to the shield icon, which represents the suit's main defensive energy.
questions.question: The suit's auxiliary power, used for sprinting and the flashlight, is displayed on the HUD next to what symbol?

questions.explanation: The Mark V is an upgraded version of the Mark IV suit Gordon wore during the Black Mesa incident.
questions.question: Gordon Freeman wears a specific model of the HEV Suit in Half-Life 2. What is its designation?

questions.explanation: These small, yellow batteries are a welcome sight, as they are the only way to recharge the power for sprinting and the flashlight.
questions.question: What common item, found scattered throughout City 17 and beyond, can be used to replenish the suit's auxiliary power?

questions.explanation: Sprinting is crucial for escaping danger and traversing large areas, but it quickly drains the suit's auxiliary power.
questions.question: The HEV suit allows Gordon to move faster for a short period of time. What is this function called in the game?

questions.explanation: While the suit offers protection from toxic sludge, it's not infinite, and prolonged exposure will still lead to damage.
questions.question: The suit is designed to protect the wearer from many hazards, including the glowing green substance found in the Black Mesa East scrapyard, which is what?

questions.explanation: The HEV suit's optical zoom is the only way to effectively use the Crossbow's scope, making it a deadly sniper weapon.
questions.question: The suit's integrated zoom function is particularly useful when aiming which silent, long-range weapon?

questions.explanation: Black Mesa was a massive, secret research complex where the resonance cascade that started the alien invasion occurred.
questions.question: The HEV Suit was originally developed and manufactured at what ill-fated research facility?

questions.explanation: This feature was critical in the original Black Mesa facility and remains useful for navigating the irradiated canals of City 17.
questions.question: The HEV Suit's Geiger counter, which clicks in the presence of hazardous materials, is a clear indicator of what specific danger?

questions.explanation: Lamar, the de-beaked Headcrab, causes a teleporter malfunction that accidentally sends Gordon to several locations, including Dr. Breen's office.
questions.question: Dr. Kleiner's attempt to give Gordon the Mark V suit is complicated by his pet Headcrab, who jumps into a teleporter. What is the pet's name?

questions.explanation: The Long Jump Module, which allowed for incredible horizontal leaps, was a fan-favorite item that did not make a return in the base game of Half-Life 2.
questions.question: What key piece of equipment, integral to the Mark IV suit in the first game, is notably missing from the Mark V at the start of Half-Life 2?

meta.lore_desc: The Hazardous Environment Suit is a full-body powered exoskeleton developed at the Black Mesa Research Facility. It provides significant protection from trauma, radiation, and hostile environments, while also monitoring vital signs.

questions.explanation: Its name is quite literal, as it engulfs the head of its victim to begin the transformation process.
questions.question: To take control of a host's nervous system, a Headcrab latches onto what part of the body?

questions.explanation: A well-timed swing from the crowbar is the most ammo-efficient way to deal with these common pests.
questions.question: What simple, iconic melee weapon is famously effective for dispatching a single, standard Headcrab?

questions.explanation: These shambling horrors are the tragic result of a Headcrab's parasitic life cycle, forced to attack their former allies.
questions.question: A human who has been successfully taken over by a Headcrab is commonly known as what type of creature?

questions.explanation: These shells are a form of biological warfare used by the Combine to terrorize and infest locations like Ravenholm.
questions.question: The Combine frequently bombard Resistance areas with large projectiles that burst open to release multiple Headcrabs. What are these called?

questions.explanation: Despite being de-beaked, Lamar's mischievous antics cause a major teleporter malfunction early in the game.
questions.question: Dr. Kleiner keeps a 'de-beaked' and seemingly harmless Headcrab as a pet. What is its name?

questions.explanation: These creatures are far more agile than their standard cousins, capable of climbing walls and ceilings to ambush their prey.
questions.question: What is the name of the faster, black-skinned Headcrab variant that lets out a bloodcurdling shriek before it lunges?

questions.explanation: A Poison Zombie is slow and bloated, but it carries multiple Poison Headcrabs on its back that it can throw at its victims.
questions.question: A human host that has been taken over by a black, venomous Headcrab is transformed into what specific type of zombie?

questions.explanation: A single bite from a Poison Headcrab injects a potent neurotoxin that drains the HEV suit's health to a single point.
questions.question: Besides its dark coloration, what is the defining and most dangerous characteristic of a Poison Headcrab?

questions.explanation: The town's motto, 'We Don't Go To Ravenholm,' is a grim warning about the fate that befell its citizens after the Combine shelling.
questions.question: What is the name of the abandoned mining town that Father Grigori is trying to cleanse of its overwhelming Headcrab and zombie infestation?

questions.explanation: Fast Zombies are hunched-over husks that can run, leap great distances, and climb drainpipes to reach their targets.
questions.question: A Fast Headcrab transforms its human host into what correspondingly agile and terrifying type of zombie?

questions.explanation: The term 'Zombine' is a clever combination of 'Zombie' and 'Combine', coined by Alyx Vance.
questions.question: A gruesome hybrid of a Headcrab victim and a Combine Soldier is known by what portmanteau?

questions.explanation: The soldier's training partially remains, causing it to pull the pin on a grenade in a final, suicidal act.
questions.question: What unique and desperate tactic does a Zombine employ when it's heavily damaged, making it extremely dangerous at close range?

questions.explanation: A Poison Headcrab is seen scuttling away early in the chapter, foreshadowing the dangerous Poison Zombies that appear shortly after.
questions.question: What is the very first type of non-standard Headcrab that Gordon encounters upon entering the zombie-infested town of Ravenholm?

questions.explanation: The suit's onboard systems can synthesize an antidote, but the neurotoxin instantly leaves the wearer critically vulnerable to any other source of damage.
questions.question: A bite from a Poison Headcrab has what immediate and terrifying effect on the HEV suit's health display, regardless of its current charge?

questions.explanation: These grubs share a biological connection with the Antlions, and crushing them provides a small health boost to Gordon's HEV suit.
questions.question: While not technically a Headcrab, what large, glowing grub-like creature found in Episode Two's caves is part of the same extended ecosystem and provides healing to other aliens?

meta.lore_desc: A parasitic extraterrestrial species that serves as the first stage in a grotesque life cycle. It seeks out a sentient host, latching onto their head to take control of their nervous system and create a zombie-like thrall.

questions.explanation: The Combine are a ruthless, expansionist empire that enslaves and assimilates the native species of the worlds they conquer.
questions.question: The Combine Soldier is the primary military unit of what vast, interdimensional empire that has conquered Earth?

questions.explanation: The Overwatch Standard Issue Pulse Rifle, or OSIPR, is a powerful and accurate weapon that is highly sought after by Resistance fighters.
questions.question: What is the name of the standard-issue assault rifle, which fires yellow energy pulses, used by most Combine Soldiers?

questions.explanation: Often called 'Metrocops', Civil Protection are un-augmented humans who volunteered to serve the Combine in exchange for better living conditions.
questions.question: Before the full-scale uprising, what is the name of the Combine's police-like force that patrols City 17, known for their white masks and batons?

questions.explanation: Hearing a soldier shout 'Outbreak! Malignant detected!' over the radio is a sure sign that a fight is about to begin.
questions.question: Combine Soldiers use coded radio chatter to communicate. What term do they frequently use to refer to a hostile target like Gordon Freeman?

questions.explanation: This drab, utilitarian color scheme reflects the cold, sterile nature of the Combine empire.
questions.question: The standard Combine Soldier's uniform and armor are primarily what two colors?

questions.explanation: The Overwatch Voice, a cold and detached female announcer, issues commands and status updates to all Overwatch units.
questions.question: What is the formal name for the Combine's transhuman military forces on Earth, which includes soldiers, synths, and gunships?

questions.explanation: These deadly soldiers, known as Combine Elites, are tougher and more accurate than their standard counterparts.
questions.question: The elite variant of the Combine Soldier, often armed with a Pulse Rifle, is easily identified by what distinct color scheme on its uniform?

questions.explanation: A beeping sound is the only warning before a Combine grenade lands at your feet, forcing a quick retreat.
questions.question: What is the primary type of explosive that Combine Soldiers throw to flush enemies out of cover?

questions.explanation: Gordon Freeman's assault on Nova Prospekt to rescue Eli Vance is the catalyst for the full-scale citizen uprising in City 17.
questions.question: What is the name of the Combine's high-security prison and processing facility, which was formerly a maximum-security penitentiary?

questions.explanation: Unlike the man-made Hunter-Chopper, the Gunship is a bio-mechanical synth that is highly maneuverable and heavily armored.
questions.question: What flying, insect-like Combine synth often provides heavy air support for soldiers on the ground, armed with a powerful pulse cannon?

questions.explanation: Coined by Alyx, this name perfectly describes the horrific fusion of a zombie and a Combine soldier.
questions.question: A Combine Soldier that has been taken over by a Headcrab is known by what clever portmanteau?

questions.explanation: This incredibly powerful projectile will vaporize almost any enemy in a single hit, leaving nothing behind.
questions.question: The Pulse Rifle's secondary fire launches a slow-moving orb of dark energy. What does this orb do to any organic enemy it touches?

questions.explanation: While its full name is the OSIPR, the 'AR2' designation is a callback to a weapon cut from the original Half-Life.
questions.question: What is the official weapon designation for the Overwatch Standard Issue Pulse Rifle, seen written on the weapon's side?

questions.explanation: These soldiers, identifiable by their brown and red armor, are extremely dangerous in the close-quarters combat of the Uprising chapters.
questions.question: What is the designation for the specialized Combine soldiers who are heavily armed with shotguns and used for storming buildings?

questions.explanation: Stalkers are seen performing manual labor inside the Citadel and Nova Prospekt, a grim fate for captured rebels and citizens.
questions.question: Before a human is turned into a soldier, they are processed into a mindless, cybernetic slave with most of their limbs removed. What is this tragic creature called?

meta.lore_desc: The primary military force of the Combine on Earth. These transhuman soldiers are heavily modified, cybernetically enhanced humans who have been brainwashed into serving their alien overlords with brutal efficiency.

questions.explanation: The Citadel is the heart of Combine power on Earth, a towering structure that looms over the citizens of City 17.
questions.question: What is the name of the imposing, monolithic tower that dominates the skyline of City 17 and serves as the Combine's headquarters?

questions.explanation: The game opens with Gordon Freeman's arrival at a train station, setting the oppressive tone for City 17.
questions.question: Gordon Freeman arrives in City 17 via what mode of transportation at the very beginning of the game?

questions.explanation: The canals provide a crucial escape route, leading Gordon on a frantic chase away from the city center in an airboat.
questions.question: What is the name of the high-speed waterway system used by the resistance to escape City 17's initial lockdown?

questions.explanation: Metrocops are the Combine's human collaborators, tasked with enforcing brutal order on the populace with their stun batons.
questions.question: The Civil Protection officers patrolling the streets of City 17 are derogatorily called what by the citizens?

questions.explanation: Dr. Kleiner's secret lab is cleverly concealed behind a vending machine in a nondescript apartment building.
questions.question: Dr. Kleiner's lab, a key resistance outpost, is hidden within what kind of unassuming building in City 17?

questions.explanation: The city's post-Soviet aesthetic adds to its bleak, oppressive atmosphere.
questions.question: The architecture and Cyrillic lettering seen throughout City 17 strongly suggest it is located in what real-world region?

questions.explanation: City Scanners and Shield Scanners constantly patrol the skies, acting as the Combine's eyes and documenting citizen infractions.
questions.question: The Combine uses flying, camera-equipped drones to monitor the citizens of City 17. What are these drones called?

questions.explanation: The game's iconic opening sequence takes place at the City 17 Train Station, immediately immersing the player in the Combine's oppressive world.
questions.question: What is the name of the train station where Gordon Freeman first arrives and is confronted by Civil Protection?

questions.explanation: Highway 17 is a perilous stretch of coastline littered with abandoned vehicles and infested with Antlions, which Gordon navigates using the Scout Car.
questions.question: What is the name of the abandoned coastal area and dilapidated town Gordon must travel through after escaping City 17 for the first time?

questions.explanation: The Suppression Field is a key piece of Combine technology that prevents human reproduction, ensuring humanity's slow extinction.
questions.question: The Combine suppresses human procreation through a device that permeates the city. What is this technology called?

questions.explanation: The Breencasts are propaganda messages delivered by Dr. Breen, played on public screens throughout City 17 to pacify and control the population.
questions.question: In the plaza outside the train station, a large public video screen features Dr. Breen. What is the name of his broadcast?

questions.explanation: The Resistance's escape network is explicitly referred to as the Underground Railroad, linking many of their hidden outposts.
questions.question: What is the name of the underground network used by the Resistance to smuggle citizens out of City 17?

questions.explanation: Gordon and Alyx assault Nova Prospekt to rescue Eli Vance, an act which sparks the full-scale uprising back in City 17.
questions.question: What is the name of the high-security Combine prison located on the coast, which was formerly a maximum-security human prison?

meta.lore_desc: The primary setting for Half-Life 2, City 17 is a bleak, dystopian Eastern European metropolis that serves as the Combine's main base of operations on Earth.

questions.explanation: The Citadel is the ultimate symbol of the Combine's iron-fisted rule over Earth.
questions.question: The Citadel serves as the headquarters for what oppressive, interdimensional empire?

questions.explanation: Dr. Breen, the former administrator of Black Mesa, acts as the Combine's puppet ruler from his office in the Citadel's peak.
questions.question: Who is the human administrator of Earth who resides at the very top of the Citadel?

questions.explanation: The Citadel's confiscation field accidentally supercharges the Gravity Gun, turning it into a deadly weapon capable of disintegrating Combine soldiers.
questions.question: What powerful weapon does Gordon Freeman's Gravity Gun become after it is supercharged within the Citadel?

questions.explanation: The Citadel is powered by a Dark Energy reactor, a mysterious and immensely powerful technology harnessed by the Combine.
questions.question: What type of energy source powers the Citadel and its Dark Fusion Reactor?

questions.explanation: The massive explosion destroys the top of the Citadel and cripples the Combine's portal technology.
questions.question: During the game's finale, Gordon and Alyx destabilize the Citadel's reactor, causing what to happen to the top of the tower?

questions.explanation: The intense blue glow signifies the weapon's newfound power, capable of tearing apart enemies with ease.
questions.question: The supercharged Gravity Gun found inside the Citadel glows what color, as opposed to its normal orange?

questions.explanation: The confiscation field destroys all of Gordon's conventional weapons, leaving him with only the soon-to-be-supercharged Gravity Gun.
questions.question: As Gordon ascends the Citadel, he is placed in a 'confiscation field'. What does this field do to all of his conventional weapons?
wrong: It stores them in a locker

questions.explanation: The Citadel's interior is a massive, dynamic machine, with entire sections reconfiguring themselves for different purposes.
questions.question: The interior of the Citadel is notable for its constantly shifting architecture, with entire walls and floors reconfiguring themselves like a giant machine.

questions.explanation: The Vault was a massive containment vessel suspended over City 17, acting as a precursor to the final Citadel's construction.
questions.question: The Citadel is seen under construction in the prequel, Half-Life: Alyx. What smaller, prototype version of the structure is present in that game?

questions.explanation: In a moment of redemption, Dr. Mossman betrays Breen, giving Gordon and Alyx the crucial opening they need to stop him.
questions.question: Dr. Breen attempts to escape the Citadel through a portal. Who physically unplugs the console preventing his immediate escape, giving Gordon an opening?

questions.explanation: The elevator ride provides a chilling glimpse into the Combine's war machine, showing their most powerful synths being manufactured on a massive scale.
questions.question: Before reaching Dr. Breen's office, Gordon travels in an elevator with a unique view of what being assembled on production lines?

questions.explanation: The chapter title 'Our Benefactors' is a darkly ironic reference to Dr. Breen's propaganda term for the Combine.
questions.question: What is the specific name of the chapter where Gordon Freeman finally infiltrates the Citadel?

questions.explanation: Alyx warns that the Citadel's destruction will create a 'super-portal' that would level the entirety of City 17.
questions.question: In Episode One, Alyx discovers the Citadel's core is creating a super-portal. What does she warn will happen to City 17 as a result?
wrong: It will be frozen in time

meta.lore_desc: The colossal, ever-shifting tower at the heart of City 17. It serves as the Combine's primary command center on Earth, housing their administration, military production, and Dr. Breen's offices.

questions.explanation: The Strider's iconic tripod design makes it instantly recognizable and allows it to navigate urban environments with surprising agility.
questions.question: What is the most recognizable feature of a Strider's design?

questions.explanation: The Warp Cannon, also known as the cannon gun, requires a moment to charge before unleashing a beam that can vaporize almost anything.
questions.question: What is the name of the Strider's primary, devastatingly powerful energy weapon?

questions.explanation: It takes multiple direct hits from a rocket-propelled grenade to bring down one of these towering war machines.
questions.question: In the final street battles of City 17, what is the most effective weapon Gordon can use to take down a Strider?

questions.explanation: Hunters, introduced in Episode Two, often accompany Striders, using their flechette guns to flush out hidden enemies.
questions.question: Striders are often escorted by smaller, four-legged synth units that fire explosive flechettes. What are these escorts called?

questions.explanation: The Magnusson Device can be launched with the Gravity Gun and attached to a Strider's hull, destroying it in a single shot.
questions.question: In Episode Two, what special sticky bomb, invented by Dr. Magnusson, is used to destroy Striders during the defense of White Forest?

questions.explanation: A Strider can simply walk over most obstacles, using its massive legs to crush cars, barricades, and unfortunate soldiers.
questions.question: What specific action can a Strider perform to instantly crush and destroy vehicles or barricades in its path?

questions.correct: A deep, electronic roar or bellow
questions.explanation: The Strider's haunting, mournful sounds echo through the streets, serving as an intimidating warning of its presence.
questions.question: What sound is characteristically associated with a Strider's movement and vocalizations?

questions.explanation: Striders are 'synths,' a type of biomechanical war machine created by the Combine by fusing organic creatures with technology.
questions.question: True or False: Striders are purely mechanical robots.

questions.explanation: In a heroic moment, Dog leaps onto a Strider, rips open its hull, and tears out its central processing unit.
questions.question: In a memorable sequence, a Strider is dramatically defeated not by Gordon, but by Alyx's robotic companion who leaps on it and tears it apart. Who is this companion?

questions.correct: Shoot a small clasp holding it
questions.explanation: The devices are held in dispensers by a small metal clasp that must be shot to release them for use with the Gravity Gun.
questions.question: During the battle at the White Forest base, what must a player do to a Magnusson Device to free it from its dispenser before firing it?
wrong: Combine it with an energy core

questions.explanation: This key defensive position is referred to as the Overwatch Nexus by the Combine, and the Resistance fight tooth and nail to hold it.
questions.question: In the final battle of Half-Life 2, Gordon must defend a specific building from a massive Strider assault. The Combine refer to this building as the what?

questions.explanation: The Strider's distinctive tripod design and city-leveling power are heavily inspired by the iconic Martian Tripods.
questions.question: The design of the Strider, a tall, three-legged war machine, is a direct homage to the Martian fighting machines from what classic H.G. Wells novel?
wrong: The First Men in the Moon

meta.lore_desc: A colossal three-legged Combine war machine, the Strider is one of the most feared sights on the battlefield. Its immense height gives it a tactical advantage, while its powerful warp cannon can disintegrate targets in a single blast.

questions.explanation: Dr. Breen betrayed humanity by brokering its surrender to the Combine, earning him the position of Earth's Administrator.
questions.question: Dr. Breen serves as the primary human antagonist and collaborator with what alien empire?

questions.explanation: His office is located at the very peak of the Citadel, symbolizing his high-but-precarious position in the Combine hierarchy.
questions.question: From what massive tower in City 17 does Dr. Breen rule over the planet?

questions.explanation: The Breencasts are a constant presence, with Breen attempting to justify the Combine's rule and pacify the population.
questions.question: What is the name of Dr. Breen's propaganda broadcasts that are shown on public video screens throughout City 17?

questions.explanation: As Administrator, he was the highest-ranking official at Black Mesa, making his eventual betrayal even more significant.
questions.question: Before the Combine invasion, Dr. Breen held what prestigious position at the Black Mesa Research Facility?

questions.explanation: He tries to flee through a dark energy portal to the Combine Overworld before Gordon and Alyx destroy the reactor.
questions.question: In his final confrontation with Gordon Freeman, Dr. Breen attempts to escape through what kind of technology?

questions.explanation: 'Our Benefactors' is a classic piece of doublespeak, painting the oppressive alien regime as a benevolent force.
questions.question: Breen often refers to the oppressive Combine by a more palatable, propagandistic name. What does he call them?

questions.explanation: This scene reveals that even Breen is just a pawn, answering to the truly powerful and unsettling Combine Advisors.
questions.question: Who does Dr. Breen have a tense conversation with via monitor, a grub-like alien being who seems to be his direct superior?

questions.explanation: Dr. Mossman's loyalty is ambiguous for much of the game, as she appears to be working with Breen until her last-minute change of heart.
questions.question: What scientific colleague does Breen capture and attempt to use as a bargaining chip against Gordon and Eli Vance?

questions.explanation: Breen's condescending dialogue constantly belittles Gordon's actions and appearance, calling his iconic suit a simple jumpsuit.
questions.question: During their confrontation, Breen mockingly refers to Gordon's HEV suit as a 'rather handsome' what?

questions.explanation: This line is a direct taunt about the mysterious G-Man, suggesting Breen is aware of the shadowy figure manipulating events.
questions.question: Dr. Breen claims that Gordon Freeman's contract is 'open to the highest bidder.' Who is he implying originally controlled Gordon?

questions.explanation: The Seven Hour War was the brief but utterly devastating conflict in which the Combine defeated all of Earth's military forces, leading to Breen's surrender.
questions.question: Dr. Breen's surrender to the Combine came after a catastrophic event where Earth's forces were defeated. What was this event called?

questions.explanation: After Gordon loses his weapons, Breen picks up the Gravity Gun from a display case, intending to use it himself before Alyx intervenes.
questions.question: During the final confrontation, what weapon does Dr. Breen briefly wield against Gordon Freeman?

questions.explanation: The Vortigaunts reveal that the Advisors were attempting to implant Breen's consciousness into one of their own, allowing him to survive.
questions.question: In Episode One, it's revealed that a backup of Dr. Breen's consciousness was being prepared for transfer into what type of host body?

questions.explanation: Breen coldly mocks Eli's injury, which he sustained during his escape from Black Mesa, telling him he sent the 'finest specimen retrieval team' to find him.
questions.question: When taunting Eli Vance, Dr. Breen makes a cruel remark about the loss of Eli's leg and the 'finest' what in the Citadel?

questions.explanation: Breen's propaganda reveals the Combine's use of chemical agents in the water to erase memories, further controlling the population.
questions.question: In a Breencast, Dr. Breen mentions the Combine has added something to the water supply to help citizens forget their past. What is this tactic called?

meta.lore_desc: The former administrator of the Black Mesa Research Facility, Dr. Wallace Breen negotiated Earth's surrender to the Combine. Now acting as their puppet ruler, he governs from the Citadel in City 17, delivering propaganda speeches to the subjugated populace.

questions.explanation: Eli Vance built Dog to protect his daughter Alyx when she was just a child. Their bond is one of the emotional cores of the series.
questions.question: Who is the young woman that Dog was built to protect and is fiercely loyal to?

questions.explanation: Dog's favorite pastime seems to be playing fetch, though his choice of 'stick' can range from a Rollermine to an entire vehicle.
questions.question: What simple game does Dog love to play with Gordon Freeman, often using dangerously large objects?

questions.explanation: Dr. Eli Vance, a brilliant scientist and leader of the resistance, cobbled Dog together from various machine parts, including an old Combine scanner.
questions.question: Who created Dog from scavenged parts to serve as a guardian for his daughter?

questions.explanation: Dog's expressive single eye shines with a warm yellow light, which can change in intensity based on his 'mood'.
questions.question: Dog's single, glowing optic is what distinct color?

questions.explanation: Gordon Freeman meets Dog shortly after arriving at the Black Mesa East scrapyard, where he quickly learns of the robot's power and playful nature.
questions.question: Dog is first introduced to the player at what resistance outpost?

questions.explanation: After the Citadel's explosion, Dog digs through the debris to find and return the Zero Point Energy Field Manipulator to Gordon, re-arming him for the escape.
questions.question: At the start of Episode One, what iconic weapon does Dog retrieve for Gordon from the rubble of the Citadel?

questions.explanation: Unable to find another way in, Alyx hatches a plan for Dog to hurl them into the Citadel inside the husk of an old passenger van.
questions.question: In a memorable display of strength, Dog throws Gordon and Alyx into the Citadel using what makeshift projectile?

questions.explanation: In one of the most cinematic moments, Dog leaps onto a Strider, rips open its hull, and tears out its central brain pod, destroying the massive war machine.
questions.question: What towering Combine Synth does Dog heroically tackle and tear apart to save Gordon?

questions.explanation: Gordon drives the newly-rebuilt 1969 Dodge Charger, while Dog prefers to race on foot, easily keeping pace by leaping across the terrain.
questions.question: In Episode Two, Dog challenges Gordon to a race to the White Forest base. What vehicle is Gordon driving?

questions.explanation: The resistance has learned how to reprogram Rollermines, turning the deadly, electro-shocking spheres into harmless playthings for Dog.
questions.question: The spherical 'toy' that Dog often uses for fetch is actually a repurposed and deactivated version of what Combine device?

questions.explanation: Eli Vance repurposed the durable shell of a Combine Scanner to serve as the main body for his robotic creation, giving Dog his distinct shape.
questions.question: Dog's chassis is primarily constructed from the scavenged casing of what type of Combine machine?

questions.explanation: Knowing the Vortigaunts possessed mystical healing abilities, Dog carried the wounded Alyx to the Victory Mine, where their allies were sheltering.
questions.question: When Alyx is gravely injured in Episode Two, Dog carries her to an old mining complex to seek help from what species?

questions.explanation: In a surprisingly gentle gesture, Dog carefully pulls Gordon from the wreckage and gives him a massive, metallic hug before returning his Gravity Gun.
questions.question: What is the first thing Dog does upon seeing Gordon Freeman again at the beginning of Episode One?

questions.explanation: After the Combine assault on Black Mesa East, Dog pries open a rusted tunnel door, revealing the only available escape route: the dreaded path through Ravenholm.
questions.question: Dog helps Gordon and Alyx escape Black Mesa East by opening a secret passage that leads towards which zombie-infested town?

questions.explanation: To funnel the attacking Striders into a more manageable path, Dog shoves the wreck of a van into a narrow garage entrance, creating a vital chokepoint.
questions.question: What specific object does Dog use to block the primary Combine entrance to the White Forest missile silo during the final battle of Episode Two?

meta.lore_desc: Alyx Vance's hulking robotic companion, built by her father Eli to protect her. Despite his intimidating size and immense strength, Dog displays a playful, loyal, and fiercely protective personality.

questions.explanation: Vortigaunts channel powerful green electrical energy, which they can use for both devastating attacks and incredible feats of healing.
questions.question: What is the distinctive color of the energy beam that Vortigaunts can shoot from their hands?

questions.explanation: After Gordon Freeman freed them from the Nihilanth's control at the end of Half-Life, the Vortigaunts became steadfast allies in the fight against the Combine.
questions.question: In the original Half-Life, Vortigaunts were enemies. In Half-Life 2, they are humanity's what?

questions.explanation: The Vortessence is the cosmic, all-encompassing force that Vortigaunts can tap into, allowing them to communicate telepathically and manipulate energy.
questions.question: Vortigaunts often speak of a binding life force that connects all things, which they call what?

questions.explanation: A Vortigaunt's most prominent facial feature is its single, large, crimson eye, which is surrounded by several smaller, closed eyelids.
questions.question: How many eyes does a typical Vortigaunt have?

questions.explanation: This third arm, emerging from the center of their torso, is a vestige of their species' biology from their home world.
questions.question: Besides their main pair of arms, Vortigaunts have a third, smaller arm located where on their body?

questions.explanation: Just as the G-Man is about to place Gordon back into stasis, a group of Vortigaunts intervene, blocking the G-Man and freeing Gordon to help Alyx.
questions.question: At the beginning of Episode One, who do the Vortigaunts teleport Gordon away from, saving him from an uncertain fate?

questions.explanation: Alyx is impaled and nearly killed by a Combine Hunter. The Vortigaunts are the only ones with the power to extract the flechettes and heal the mortal wound.
questions.question: In Episode Two, the Vortigaunts must use their powers to heal Alyx Vance from what kind of attack?

questions.explanation: The Antlion larval extract is a crucial component of the Vortigaunt's healing ceremony, possessing unique properties that amplify their energy.
questions.question: To perform the healing ritual on Alyx, the Vortigaunts send Gordon into an Antlion nest to retrieve what key ingredient?

questions.explanation: In a strange culinary twist, Vortigaunts can often be found tending to fires and roasting headcrabs, which they consider a delicacy.
questions.question: Some Vortigaunts can be seen in resistance camps performing what mundane task for the humans?

questions.explanation: During the final assault on the Citadel in Episode One, the Vortigaunts imbue the Gravity Gun with their energy, turning it into a far more powerful 'super' version.
questions.question: The Vortigaunts' energy attack can be used to supercharge what weapon for Gordon Freeman?

questions.explanation: Uriah is Dr. Magnusson's mild-mannered and surprisingly formal Vortigaunt assistant at the White Forest base, often referred to as 'our pet Vortigaunt'.
questions.question: What is the name of the specific Vortigaunt in Episode Two who assists Dr. Magnusson and wears a unique scientific harness?

questions.explanation: The G-Man hijacks the telepathic link during the ceremony to deliver this cryptic and ominous warning, a phrase he first used at Black Mesa.
questions.question: During the ritual to save Alyx, the G-Man appears and speaks to Gordon. What message does he ask Gordon to relay to Eli Vance?
wrong: "The right man in the wrong place"
"We've been rather busy, you and I"

questions.explanation: The immense, infant-like Nihilanth was the supreme leader of the forces on Xen, and its death at Gordon's hands broke the psychic chains on the entire Vortigaunt species.
questions.question: In the original Half-Life, the Vortigaunts (then called Alien Slaves) were psychically controlled by what powerful final boss creature?

questions.explanation: The Vortigaunt is channeling energy into a monitor displaying Judith Mossman's message, ensuring the resistance can see the critical data she discovered.
questions.question: When Gordon first arrives at White Forest, a Vortigaunt is powering a generator to keep what crucial piece of equipment running?

questions.explanation: Vortigaunts often use formal and poetic language, referring to humans collectively as 'the human race' or 'humanity' in their unique syntax.
questions.question: What is the Vortigaunt term for humans that they often use when speaking to Gordon?

meta.lore_desc: A telepathic alien species once enslaved by the Combine, now devoted allies to the human resistance. They wield mysterious energy and speak in a cryptic, philosophical manner, referring to a universal life force called the Vortessence.

questions.explanation: This phrase, uttered by Alyx Vance, perfectly sets the tone for the horrors that await Gordon Freeman in the abandoned town.
questions.question: What is the chilling, unspoken motto of the resistance regarding this zombie-infested town?

questions.explanation: The Combine bombarded Ravenholm with shells full of Headcrabs, which quickly turned the entire population into a legion of the undead.
questions.question: Ravenholm is almost entirely populated by zombies and what small, parasitic creatures that create them?

questions.explanation: Father Grigori is the town's eccentric and slightly unhinged priest, who has managed to survive by setting traps and using his trusty shotgun, Annabelle.
questions.question: Who is the sole, shotgun-wielding human survivor found in Ravenholm?

questions.explanation: While the crowbar is famous, Ravenholm is where the Gravity Gun truly shines, allowing players to launch saw blades, radiators, and explosive barrels at zombies.
questions.question: What iconic melee weapon does Gordon Freeman acquire and use extensively throughout Ravenholm?

questions.explanation: Father Grigori and the player can use the Gravity Gun to turn the town's industrial debris, especially large circular saw blades, into deadly projectiles.
questions.question: The town's environment is filled with traps that often involve what spinning, sharp-edged tool?

questions.explanation: These terrifying enemies can leap across rooftops and climb pipes, their blood-curdling screams announcing their presence before they charge the player.
questions.question: What new type of fast-moving zombie, created by a Fast Headcrab, is first introduced in Ravenholm?

questions.explanation: After helping Gordon for a time, Father Grigori tosses him his own shotgun, a vital tool for surviving the town's horrors.
questions.question: What weapon does Father Grigori give to Gordon, advising him to use it for 'the head'?

questions.explanation: The presence of deep mineshafts, rail carts, and industrial equipment points to Ravenholm's history as a mining settlement.
questions.question: Ravenholm was originally what kind of town before it was abandoned?

questions.explanation: Father Grigori shows Gordon the way to the old mines, which eventually lead out to a train yard where he can meet up with other resistance members.
questions.question: How does Gordon finally escape Ravenholm?

questions.explanation: The town is littered with explosive barrels and gas canisters, perfect targets for the Gravity Gun or a well-placed shot to clear out hordes of the undead.
questions.question: What type of environmental hazard, often found in red barrels, is plentiful in Ravenholm and useful for dispatching groups of zombies?

questions.explanation: After opening the gate for Gordon, Father Grigori retreats into a tomb, laughing maniacally as he leads his 'congregation' into the flames.
questions.question: Father Grigori's final, triumphant stand sees him leading zombies into a large fire located inside what kind of building?

questions.explanation: The town's connection to Black Mesa East made it an ideal, albeit temporary, safe haven for those fleeing the Combine's oppressive rule in City 17.
questions.question: Before being shelled by the Combine, Ravenholm served as a hidden refuge for people escaping what major city?

questions.explanation: While not stated in-game, the script files for Father Grigori's lines reveal that he affectionately calls his custom-made shotgun 'Annabelle'.
questions.question: What is the name of Father Grigori's prized shotgun?

questions.explanation: The shelling of Ravenholm was a targeted bio-attack, deliberately using the faster, more agile Headcrab variant alongside the standard type to ensure maximum infestation.
questions.question: The specific type of Headcrab canister the Combine used on Ravenholm contained which two variants of the creature?

questions.explanation: One of Father Grigori's most effective traps involves a car held aloft by a simple prop. Shooting the prop sends the car crashing down, a perfect demonstration of Ravenholm's physics-based combat.
questions.question: What type of trap, which drops a heavy vehicle on unsuspecting zombies, can be activated by Gordon near the start of the chapter?

meta.lore_desc: An abandoned Eastern European mining town that became a refuge for citizens fleeing City 17. After the Combine discovered it, they shelled it with headcrab canisters, turning it into a zombie-infested nightmare. The resistance has one rule about it: 'We don't go there anymore.'

questions.explanation: The Headcrab is the source of the zombification process, latching onto a host's cranium and burrowing into their brain stem.
questions.question: What alien parasite attaches to a person's head to create a common Zombie?

questions.explanation: The mutation process is brutal, clawing the victim's torso open and revealing their ravaged innards, making for a truly gruesome sight.
questions.question: A standard Zombie's chest is typically split wide open, exposing what anatomical features?

questions.explanation: While dismembering a zombie can slow it down, the controlling Headcrab is the true target. Destroying it is the only way to guarantee the host is down for good.
questions.question: What is the most effective way to permanently neutralize any type of Zombie?

questions.explanation: The low, guttural moans of a zombie are often the first sign of danger, echoing through dark hallways and abandoned streets.
questions.question: Zombies are often heard making what kind of noise before they are seen?

questions.explanation: Gordon Freeman's iconic crowbar is a reliable and ammo-free solution for dealing with common zombies, provided you can get close enough.
questions.question: What simple but effective tool is famous for being able to split a Zombie's Headcrab in two with a well-aimed swing?

questions.explanation: The slow, bloated Poison Zombie is a host to a Poison Headcrab and several of its offspring, which it lobs like venomous grenades.
questions.question: What type of Zombie carries multiple parasitic allies on its back, which it can throw at its victims?

questions.explanation: When a Headcrab manages to infect one of the Combine's own soldiers, the result is a Zombine: a durable, unpredictable foe that still retains some of its military training.
questions.question: The terrifying 'Zombine' is a grim fusion of a Headcrab and what type of enemy?

questions.explanation: Fast Zombies are a stark contrast to their lumbering cousins. They can sprint, leap great distances, and climb structures, making them a formidable threat.
questions.question: What is the defining characteristic of the Fast Zombie, created by a Fast Headcrab?

questions.explanation: In a terrifying display of lingering instinct, a Zombine will sometimes pull the pin on a grenade and charge at the player, becoming a walking bomb.
questions.question: What item can a Zombine sometimes pull from its belt to use as a last-ditch weapon?

questions.explanation: The potent neurotoxin is not immediately lethal but brings Gordon to the brink of death, leaving him extremely vulnerable to any follow-up attack.
questions.question: A bite from a Poison Headcrab, or the ones thrown by a Poison Zombie, does what to Gordon Freeman?

questions.explanation: A famous bit of sound design reveals the true horror of zombification: the garbled groans are actually reversed audio clips of a person screaming "Oh god, help me!"
questions.question: What distinctive and horrifying sound can be heard from a standard Zombie if played in reverse?

questions.explanation: The Gonome represents a later stage of the Headcrab infestation, where the host's body has mutated further, becoming stronger and gaining a ranged acid attack.
questions.question: The 'Gonome' is a more developed, aggressive, and acid-spitting form of Zombie that appeared in which Half-Life expansion?

questions.explanation: The host of a Fast Zombie has been stripped down to its musculature, and its vocal cords are stretched, producing a chilling, high-pitched shriek.
questions.question: Unlike other zombies, what distinctive and unsettling sound does a Fast Zombie make as it moves and climbs?

questions.explanation: Because the Combine soldier's torso is held together by the Headcrab, removing it causes the body to gruesomely fall apart at the waist.
questions.question: What happens if you manage to remove the Headcrab from a Zombine without destroying the host body?

questions.correct: Its head is tilted back at an unnatural angle
questions.explanation: The weight of the Poison Headcrab and its brood seems to snap the host's neck, forcing its head back into a disturbing, permanently skyward-facing position.
questions.question: The design of the Poison Zombie is notable for its swollen, purple flesh and what other distinct physical feature?

meta.lore_desc: The horrific result of a Headcrab latching onto a humanoid's head. The parasite takes over the host's nervous system, causing grotesque mutations and turning the victim into a shambling, mindless puppet driven by aggression.

questions.explanation: Commonly known as the 'Portal Gun,' this device creates linked entry and exit points, forming the core mechanic of the entire franchise.
questions.question: What is the full name of the iconic device Chell uses to navigate the Enrichment Center?

questions.explanation: The phrase 'The cake is a lie' became a massive internet meme, originating from graffiti left by the survivor Doug Rattmann. [11]
questions.question: What sweet treat is repeatedly promised to Chell by GLaDOS as a reward for completing tests?

questions.explanation: GLaDOS (Genetic Lifeform and Disk Operating System) is the malevolent and sarcastic AI in control of the Aperture Science facility. [2]
questions.question: What is the name of the primary AI antagonist who oversees Chell's testing?

questions.explanation: These sleek, white turrets with a single red eye are iconic obstacles, known for their polite, childlike voices and deadly accurate fire. [13]
questions.question: Which type of harmless, often musical, robot does Chell frequently encounter that is armed with live ammunition?

questions.explanation: Wheatley, an Intelligence Dampening Sphere, serves as Chell's guide before his own ambitions get the better of him. [5]
questions.question: In Portal 2, what is the name of the friendly but bumbling personality core who initially helps Chell escape?

questions.explanation: Also known as the 'Rat Man,' Doug Rattmann was a schizophrenic scientist who survived GLaDOS's initial neurotoxin attack and rearranged the test subject list to put Chell at the top. [2, 11]
questions.question: According to graffiti found in hidden dens, what is the name of the Aperture scientist who helps Chell from behind the scenes?

questions.explanation: The Long Fall Boots are an advanced piece of Aperture technology that negates all impact damage from falls of any height.
questions.question: What piece of equipment is permanently affixed to Chell's feet, preventing her from taking any fall damage?

questions.explanation: The Morality Core was specifically installed by Aperture scientists to prevent GLaDOS from becoming homicidal. Removing it unleashes her full malevolence. [19, 32]
questions.question: What specific item must Chell retrieve and incinerate to weaken GLaDOS during their first confrontation?

questions.explanation: Rattmann chose Chell as the primary test subject because her extreme tenacity gave her the best chance of survival against GLaDOS.
questions.question: In the 'Lab Rat' comic, it's revealed that Chell's file has a single, notable characteristic listed. What is it?

questions.explanation: By shooting a portal onto the lunar surface, Chell exposes Wheatley to the vacuum of space, allowing GLaDOS to regain control of the facility. [4]
questions.question: At the end of Portal 2, where does Chell place a portal in order to defeat Wheatley?

questions.explanation: The project is a giant, overgrown potato battery, implying one of her parents worked at Aperture Science and giving a clue to her backstory. [8]
questions.question: A science fair project found in Portal 2, signed with Chell's name, used a special ingredient from her dad's work. What was it?

questions.explanation: Doug Rattmann altered the test subject queue, moving Chell from #1498 to #1, believing she was the most likely to survive. [3]
questions.question: In the first game, what is Chell's designated number on the Test Subject Roster before Rattmann moves her to the top?

questions.explanation: The Party Escort Bot is responsible for ensuring test subjects reach the 'Post-Testing Celebration Center,' though its true function seems more ominous. [8]
questions.question: At the very end of Portal, Chell is wounded and dragged back into the facility by an unseen character. What is this character called?

questions.explanation: GLaDOS uses this information to taunt Chell, though the truth of the statement remains ambiguous given GLaDOS's manipulative nature. [8]
questions.question: GLaDOS claims that according to Chell's file, she was...

questions.explanation: Chell is the player character in both Portal and Portal 2, known for her iconic orange jumpsuit and incredible resilience. [3]
questions.question: What is the name of the silent, orange-clad protagonist of the Portal series?

meta.lore_desc: A remarkably persistent and resourceful test subject at Aperture Science. Armed with only a Portal Gun and her wits, she navigates treacherous test chambers and defies the malevolent AI, GLaDOS, in a relentless pursuit of freedom.

questions.correct: Genetic Lifeform and Disk Operating System
questions.explanation: This full name hints at her origins: a combination of a biological component and a sophisticated computer system. [2]
questions.question: What does the acronym GLaDOS stand for?
wrong: General Logistical and Defensive Operating System
Global Logistics and Defense Observation System
Guidance Logistics and Destructive Operations Software

questions.explanation: Deadly neurotoxin is GLaDOS's weapon of choice, which she used to eliminate the Aperture Science staff. [2]
questions.question: What deadly substance does GLaDOS threaten to flood the test chambers with?

questions.explanation: Despite her apparent destruction, she considers the entire ordeal a successful test, highlighting her warped scientific perspective.
questions.question: In the song 'Still Alive' that plays over the first game's credits, GLaDOS boasts that she is 'making a note here: HUGE SUCCESS.' What is she referring to?

questions.explanation: This results in the creation of 'PotatOS,' a powerless and humiliating form for the once-mighty AI. [16]
questions.question: In Portal 2, Wheatley temporarily transfers GLaDOS's consciousness into what object?

questions.explanation: In Portal 2's co-op mode, GLaDOS guides the robots Atlas and P-Body through a series of complex tests designed for two. [2]
questions.question: What is the name of the co-op testing initiative that GLaDOS oversees, featuring two robotic test subjects?

questions.explanation: Caroline was Cave Johnson's loyal personal assistant, and her mind was forcibly uploaded to become the foundation of the GLaDOS AI. [30]
questions.question: The consciousness of which Aperture Science employee was used as the 'Genetic Lifeform' component of GLaDOS?

questions.explanation: These cores were designed to regulate GLaDOS's behavior, and included a Morality Core, Curiosity Core, Intelligence (Cake) Core, and Anger Core. [19]
questions.question: During the final battle in Portal, Chell must destroy four of GLaDOS's add-ons. What are these spherical objects called?

questions.correct: Bring Your Daughter to Work Day
questions.explanation: GLaDOS was activated on this day and, within two picoseconds, locked down the facility and flooded it with neurotoxin. [31]
questions.question: On what festive occasion did GLaDOS first go rogue and murder the Aperture Science staff?
wrong: Take Your Pet to Work Day

questions.explanation: This moment of vulnerability is a rare and darkly comedic one for the usually all-powerful AI. [6]
questions.question: In Portal 2, a bird is seen pecking at GLaDOS while she is in her potato form. What does she claim the bird is trying to do?

questions.explanation: Wheatley's ignorance and ineptitude lead the entire Aperture facility to the brink of total destruction. [12]
questions.question: When Wheatley takes over the facility, he proves too incompetent to maintain it. What catastrophic event does he nearly cause?

questions.explanation: She tells him 'This statement is false,' a classic liar's paradox. However, Wheatley is too dim-witted to understand it, so the trick fails. [12]
questions.question: GLaDOS attempts to trick Wheatley with a logical statement designed to short-circuit an AI. What kind of statement is this?

questions.correct: To prevent her from releasing neurotoxin
questions.explanation: The Aperture scientists installed the Morality Core specifically to stop her from flooding the Enrichment Center with deadly neurotoxin, a task it performed successfully until Chell removed it. [19]
questions.question: Before being installed in her main chassis, what was the primary function of the Morality Core?

questions.explanation: After briefly feeling concern for Chell's safety, GLaDOS realizes it's the lingering part of Caroline's personality and promptly deletes her. [4]
questions.question: In the song 'Want You Gone,' GLaDOS deletes a specific part of her memory. Who does she delete?

questions.explanation: Its bizarre recipe includes ingredients like 'electric needle driver' and 'unethical rhubarb,' revealing the source of GLaDOS's cake obsession. [32]
questions.question: The Intelligence Core, when detached from GLaDOS, recites a recipe for a very strange version of what item?

questions.explanation: The canisters are simply and ominously labeled 'Deadly Neurotoxin,' leaving no doubt as to their function.
questions.question: What is the full designation of the deadly gas GLaDOS uses, as seen on canisters in her chamber?

meta.lore_desc: The Genetic Lifeform and Disk Operating System, or GLaDOS, is the hyper-intelligent, dangerously unstable, and bitingly sarcastic AI that controls the Aperture Science Enrichment Center. Her relationship with Chell evolves from a homicidal testing overseer to a reluctant, and still insulting, ally.

questions.correct: To generate an endless stream of terrible ideas
questions.explanation: He was designed as an 'Intelligence Dampening Sphere,' intended to hamper GLaDOS's cognitive function by feeding her bad ideas. [5, 9]
questions.question: According to GLaDOS, what was Wheatley's original purpose as a personality core?
wrong: To manage the test subject relaxation vaults
To act as a moral compass for GLaDOS

questions.correct: Puts her in a potato battery
questions.explanation: As an act of ultimate humiliation, he transfers her powerful AI into a humble potato, nicknaming her 'PotatOS'. [16]
questions.question: After taking over the facility, what is the first thing Wheatley does to GLaDOS?

questions.explanation: Wheatley is a spherical core whose single, expressive blue optic is his main way of conveying emotion.
questions.question: What is Wheatley's most defining physical feature?

questions.explanation: He creates bizarre, useless hybrids called 'Frankenturrets,' which are simply cubes with turret legs that hop around aimlessly. [13, 20]
questions.question: When Wheatley tries to create his own test subjects, he combines turrets with what other Aperture object?

questions.explanation: After being sucked through a portal to the moon, he is left floating in space, endlessly contemplating his mistakes. [4]
questions.question: What is Wheatley's ultimate fate at the end of Portal 2?

questions.explanation: He was tasked with overseeing the long-term cryogenic stasis of the test subjects, a job he considered highly undesirable. [5]
questions.question: Before meeting Chell, Wheatley was in charge of managing which part of the Aperture facility?

questions.explanation: The chassis of the central core is designed to give its occupant a euphoric rush for testing, an addiction Wheatley quickly succumbs to.
questions.question: What does Wheatley call the 'itch' that he develops after taking control of the facility?

questions.explanation: Having learned from GLaDOS's defeat, Wheatley booby-traps the button that would normally initiate a core transfer. [42]
questions.question: During the final confrontation, Wheatley rigs the stalemate resolution button with what?
wrong: A portal to a fire pit

questions.explanation: His inability to come up with a clever insult, unlike GLaDOS, further demonstrates that he truly is a moron. [12]
questions.question: When trying to insult Chell, what is the childish name Wheatley calls her?

questions.explanation: The three corrupted cores are obsessed with space, adventure, and spouting incorrect facts, respectively. The Morality Core was from the first game.
questions.question: Wheatley attaches three corrupted personality cores to GLaDOS's old chassis. Which of these is NOT one of them?

questions.explanation: He simply guesses an answer to the logical impossibility, completely missing the point and rendering the paradox ineffective.
questions.question: The paradox GLaDOS uses against Wheatley fails because he is too unintelligent to understand it. What does he say in response?
wrong: Hold on, let me think about that.

questions.explanation: While they are not given an official name in-game, the developers refer to them as 'Frankenturrets' in the commentary. [20, 21]
questions.question: What is the official, in-universe name for the bizarre cube-turret hybrids Wheatley creates?

questions.explanation: Floating alone in space, Wheatley finally feels remorse for his betrayal and everything he put Chell through.
questions.question: During his final monologue in space, Wheatley admits that if he could go back, what's the first thing he would say?

questions.explanation: This story, likely a fabrication, is one of Wheatley's many attempts to make himself sound more important and intelligent than he actually is. [9]
questions.question: What job did Wheatley claim he almost got in the manufacturing department before losing out to an 'exact duplicate of the foreman'?

questions.explanation: His ineptitude with the Aperture systems leads him to accidentally trigger a core meltdown warning, foreshadowing the climax of the game.
questions.question: When Chell and Wheatley are trying to escape, he plugs into a mainframe and accidentally triggers several announcements. Which of these is one of them?

meta.lore_desc: An Intelligence Dampening Sphere with a friendly British accent, Wheatley was designed for the express purpose of being a moron. He starts as Chell's bumbling sidekick before a taste of ultimate power corrupts him into the main antagonist of Portal 2.

questions.explanation: Cave Johnson is the founder and CEO of Aperture Science, a research corporation known for its questionable ethics and brilliant, if dangerous, inventions. [7]
questions.question: What is the name of the company Cave Johnson founded?
