questions.question: What is the only tool that can be used to pick up a placed cake block, allowing you to move it without destroying it?

questions.explanation: Simply crafting a cake for the first time will grant the player 'The Lie' advancement, a nod to the game Portal.
questions.question: The achievement/advancement 'The Lie' is a reference to another popular video game and is awarded for doing what with a cake?
wrong: Placing it on a Redstone Block

questions.explanation: A comparator's signal strength is proportional to how full the cake is. A full cake gives a signal strength of 14, which decreases by 2 for every slice eaten.
questions.question: If a comparator is placed facing a cake, it will output a Redstone signal. What determines the strength of this signal?
wrong: How long the cake has been placed

questions.explanation: Unlike most other foods, cake can be eaten even with a full hunger bar. This makes it a less efficient, but always available, source of saturation.
questions.question: What happens if you try to eat a slice of cake when your hunger bar is already full?

questions.explanation: The Warden is a massive and destructive mob that can destroy blocks it walks through, including a placed cake.
questions.question: Which of these mobs might try to trample and destroy a cake block if they walk over it?

questions.explanation: Using an empty bucket on a Cow, Mooshroom, or Goat will yield a bucket of milk, which is a key ingredient for a cake.
questions.question: The recipe for cake requires three buckets of milk. Which farm animal must you interact with using an empty bucket to get milk?

questions.correct: They are returned to your inventory
questions.explanation: When crafting a cake, the three empty buckets are conveniently returned to the player's inventory, ready to be refilled.
questions.question: What happens to the empty buckets after you've used them to craft a cake?
wrong: They are consumed in the recipe
They are placed on the ground

questions.explanation: Placing a single candle of any color onto an uncut cake turns it into a 'Candle Cake'. It functions identically but provides a small amount of light.
questions.question: A lit candle can be placed on an uneaten cake. What does this create?

questions.explanation: This is a trick question! You can place a cake in all dimensions, including the Nether and The End. It's a reliable food source anywhere.
questions.question: What is the one dimension in the game where you cannot place a cake block on the ground?
wrong: You can place it in all dimensions

questions.explanation: Cake blocks are fragile and cannot be pushed by pistons. Attempting to do so will simply break the cake block without dropping anything.
questions.question: If you try to push a cake block with a regular piston, what is the result?
wrong: The cake is dropped as an item

questions.explanation: Pandas have unique pathfinding and will not attempt to walk over a placed cake block, unlike most other mobs.
questions.question: Which of these mobs is completely incapable of pathfinding over a placed cake block, effectively making it a tiny barrier for them?

questions.explanation: Eating a slice of cake is instantaneous, with no 'use time' or eating animation, allowing a player to restore hunger very quickly if needed.
questions.question: You can eat cake much faster than other food items in the game. What is the 'cooldown' or use time for eating one slice of cake?

meta.lore_desc: A unique, placeable food block that can be eaten slice by slice. Often crafted for celebrations, this sweet treat is made from a combination of milk, sugar, wheat, and an egg.

questions.explanation: Coal is the most common and reliable fuel source for a furnace, used for both smelting ores and cooking food.
questions.question: What common, dark mineral is the most standard type of fuel used to power a furnace?

questions.explanation: A furnace is one of the first essential items a player crafts, requiring eight cobblestone blocks.
questions.question: To craft a furnace, you need to arrange eight of which type of block in a ring on a crafting table?

questions.explanation: Smelting is the primary way to turn raw ore blocks, like iron and gold, into ingots that can be used for crafting tools and armor.
questions.question: Putting raw Iron Ore into a furnace with fuel will produce what useful item?

questions.explanation: Placing sand in the top slot of a furnace and adding fuel will smelt it into a transparent block of glass.
questions.question: Besides ores, what common block found on beaches and in deserts can be smelted in a furnace to create Glass?

questions.explanation: When you take a finished item out of a furnace's output slot, you gain a small number of experience orbs.
questions.question: Smelting items in a furnace rewards the player with a small amount of what?

questions.explanation: The Smoker is a dedicated food-cooking station, crafted from a furnace and four logs, that dramatically speeds up the process.
questions.question: Which of these is a specialized type of furnace that can only cook food, but does so twice as fast as a regular one?

questions.explanation: For players who need to process large amounts of ore quickly, the Blast Furnace is the ideal upgrade.
questions.question: What is the name of the furnace variant that smelts ores and metal-based items twice as fast, but cannot be used for cooking food?

questions.explanation: Charcoal is a renewable fuel source made by smelting wood logs. It's identical to coal in its smelting properties and can also be used to craft torches.
questions.question: If you smelt a block of wood, you get a new type of fuel that burns for the exact same duration as coal. What is it called?

questions.explanation: A single Bucket of Lava is the longest-lasting fuel in the game, smelting a whopping 100 items before being consumed, leaving an empty bucket behind.
questions.question: Which of these items is the most efficient fuel source in the game, capable of smelting 100 items per unit?

questions.explanation: The Minecart with Furnace acts as a locomotive, using coal to propel itself and push a train of other minecarts along a track.
questions.question: What is the name of the special minecart variant that has a furnace inside it and can be powered with coal to push other minecarts?

questions.explanation: To craft a Blast Furnace, you need to smelt Cobblestone into Stone, and then smelt the Stone again to get Smooth Stone.
questions.question: Crafting a Blast Furnace requires a regular furnace, five iron ingots, and three of what other material?

questions.explanation: Smelting a wet sponge will dry it out, allowing it to be used again to soak up water.
questions.question: What happens if a wet sponge is placed in the top slot of a furnace with fuel below it?

questions.explanation: Most wooden items, such as planks, logs, and crafting tables, will smelt 1.5 items each, making them a decent early-game fuel if coal is scarce.
questions.question: Which of these items, when used as fuel, will smelt exactly 1.5 items before being consumed?

questions.explanation: To automate a furnace, a Hopper on top feeds in the items to be smelted, a Hopper on the side or back feeds in fuel, and a Hopper on the bottom pulls out the finished product.
questions.question: To automate a furnace, a player can use Hoppers. To feed fuel into the furnace, which side of the block must the Hopper be attached to?

questions.explanation: An alternative to finding green dye in the world is to simply smelt a block of cactus, which yields one unit of green dye.
questions.question: Smelting Cactus in a furnace produces what item?

meta.lore_desc: An essential utility block for any survivor, the Furnace uses fuel to smelt raw ores into usable ingots, cook food to make it more nourishing, and transform various other materials into new forms.

questions.explanation: A chest is crafted using eight wooden planks of any type, leaving the center square of the crafting grid empty.
questions.question: To craft a standard chest, you need to place eight of what material in a ring on the crafting table?

questions.explanation: Two adjacent chests will merge to form a single Large Chest, which has double the storage capacity.
questions.question: Placing two standard chests directly next to each other will combine them into what?

questions.explanation: A single chest provides 27 slots for item storage, arranged in a 9x3 grid.
questions.question: How many inventory slots does a standard, single chest have?

questions.explanation: A chest needs at least one block of empty space (or a transparent block) above it for the lid to open.
questions.question: What happens if you try to open a chest that has a solid, opaque block placed directly on top of it?

questions.explanation: Tamed cats love to sit on things, and if they choose to sit on a chest, the player will be unable to open it until the cat moves.
questions.question: Which of these passive mobs has a habit of sitting on top of chests, preventing them from being opened until the mob is pushed off?

questions.explanation: The Ender Chest provides a player-specific, global inventory that can be accessed from any Ender Chest block.
questions.question: What is the name of the special, magical chest that allows you to access its inventory from any other chest of the same type, anywhere in the world?

questions.explanation: A Trapped Chest is a Redstone component that produces a signal when a player accesses its inventory, perfect for creating secret doors or traps.
questions.question: A chest that looks almost identical to a normal one but emits a Redstone signal when opened is called what?

questions.explanation: A Trapped Chest is crafted by placing a regular chest and a tripwire hook anywhere in the crafting grid.
questions.question: To craft a Trapped Chest, you need to combine a regular chest with what other Redstone-related item?

questions.explanation: An Ender Chest is crafted with an Eye of Ender in the center, surrounded by eight blocks of Obsidian.
questions.question: To craft an Ender Chest, you need eight blocks of Obsidian and what other item, which is placed in the center?

questions.explanation: Shulker Boxes are portable chests. When broken, they drop as an item and keep all the items stored inside, making them invaluable for transport.
questions.question: What is the name for the special chest-like block found in End Cities that retains its inventory even when broken and picked up?

questions.explanation: Unless mined with a pickaxe enchanted with Silk Touch, an Ender Chest will break and drop only eight blocks of Obsidian, losing the Eye of Ender.
questions.question: If you break an Ender Chest without a Silk Touch pickaxe, what does it drop?

questions.correct: The number of players viewing its inventory
questions.explanation: A Trapped Chest's signal strength is equal to the number of players currently looking inside it, from a strength of 1 up to a maximum of 15.
questions.question: The Redstone signal strength from a Trapped Chest is determined by what?

questions.explanation: Donkeys, Mules, and Llamas can all be equipped with a chest, allowing them to carry items for the player.
questions.question: You can place a chest on certain animals to use them as mobile storage. Which of these can be equipped with a chest?

questions.correct: Hold sneak while placing the second chest
questions.explanation: By sneaking (holding the crouch key) while placing the second chest, you can override the automatic merging behavior, allowing you to place two separate small chests side-by-side.
questions.question: How can you place two single chests right next to each other without them automatically combining into a large chest?
wrong: Place a block between them first

meta.lore_desc: A fundamental storage block, the Chest allows players to safely store their items and resources. Crafted from wood, these containers are essential for organizing a base and safeguarding valuable loot from being lost upon death.

questions.explanation: To craft a bed, you need three blocks of wool of the same color and three wooden planks of any type.
questions.question: What two materials are needed to craft a bed?

questions.explanation: Attempting to sleep in a bed in the Nether or The End will cause it to create a powerful explosion, a tactic often used by advanced players.
questions.question: What happens if you try to use a bed in the Nether or The End?

questions.explanation: Besides passing the night, the most important function of a bed is to set the player's respawn point to its location.
questions.question: What is the primary function of sleeping in a bed in the Overworld?

questions.explanation: Phantoms are flying hostile mobs that spawn at night and attack players who have not slept in a bed for three or more in-game days.
questions.question: Which of these mobs will appear and attack players who haven't slept for several nights?

questions.explanation: A red bed naturally generates inside every igloo, providing a ready-made spawn point for explorers in snowy biomes.
questions.question: In which naturally generated structure can you always find a red bed?

questions.explanation: Falling onto a bed will cause you to bounce and will reduce fall damage by 50%.
questions.question: Besides sleeping, what unusual physical property do beds have when you land on them?

questions.correct: Your home bed was missing or obstructed
questions.explanation: If your bed is removed or the area around it is blocked, the game will display this message and you will respawn at the original world spawn point.
questions.question: What message appears if you try to respawn but your bed has been destroyed or blocked?

questions.correct: It resets to the world spawn
questions.explanation: If your bed spawn is obstructed, you will respawn at the world spawn, and your bed spawn point is cleared. You must interact with the bed again to reset it.
questions.question: What happens to your spawn point if it is obstructed when you try to respawn?
wrong: You spawn on the nearest block

questions.explanation: In villages, baby villagers will often find beds and happily bounce on them during the daytime.
questions.question: Which of these groups of mobs can be seen bouncing on beds during the day?

questions.explanation: Before dyes could be applied to them, all beds in the game were canonically red.
questions.question: Initially, beds could only be crafted with one color of wool, resulting in only one color of bed. What was that color?

questions.explanation: Villagers always wake up on top of the bed, so if there isn't enough space above it, they can suffocate in the block above.
questions.question: If you place a solid block directly above a bed with no other space around it, what can happen to a villager who sleeps in it?

questions.explanation: Version 1.12, the 'World of Color Update', was the update that finally allowed players to dye beds into all 16 wool colors.
questions.question: Which update, also known as the 'World of Color Update', introduced the ability to craft beds in 16 different colors?

questions.explanation: For a player to safely wake up on top of the bed itself, there must be at least two full blocks of empty space above it.
questions.question: What is the minimum number of empty blocks required above a bed for a player to wake up on top of it without issue?

questions.explanation: Crying Obsidian was originally planned to be the block used for setting spawn points, but the idea was replaced by the introduction of beds.
questions.question: Before beds were introduced to set a player's spawn, which block was considered for this function?

questions.explanation: Landing on a bed reduces fall damage by half and bounces the player back up with 66% of their impact velocity.
questions.question: What percentage of fall damage is negated when a player lands on a bed?

meta.lore_desc: A fundamental block that allows players to skip the night and set their respawn point. But be warned, attempting to use it in certain dimensions has explosive consequences.

questions.explanation: The Ender Dragon is the massive, flying boss that players must defeat to 'beat' the game and open the gateway back to the Overworld.
questions.question: What is the name of the primary boss mob found in The End?

questions.explanation: The End is primarily composed of large, floating islands made of a unique, pale-yellow block called End Stone.
questions.question: What is the primary block that makes up the islands of The End?

questions.explanation: Players must place up to 12 Eyes of Ender into the End Portal Frame blocks found in a Stronghold to activate the portal.
questions.question: What item must be placed in a portal frame to activate the portal to The End?

questions.explanation: The End is the home dimension of the Endermen, and they spawn here in large numbers.
questions.question: Which tall, passive mob that becomes hostile when looked at is commonly found here?

questions.explanation: Upon the Ender Dragon's defeat, an Exit Portal (also called the End Fountain) activates, allowing the player to return to the Overworld and watch the credits.
questions.question: After defeating the Ender Dragon, what structure appears in the center of the main island?

questions.explanation: End Cities are tall, branching structures found on the outer islands, filled with valuable loot and guarded by Shulkers.
questions.question: What are the tall, city-like structures found on the outer islands of The End called?

questions.explanation: Shulkers are mobs that disguise themselves as blocks and guard the treasures of End Cities by shooting projectiles that cause the 'Levitation' status effect.
questions.question: Which purple, box-shaped mob, found in End Cities, shoots levitating projectiles?

questions.explanation: The End Ship is a rare structure that has a chance to spawn next to an End City, containing some of the game's best loot.
questions.question: What is the name of the rare, flying ship-like structure that can generate alongside an End City?

questions.explanation: Eating a Chorus Fruit will teleport the player to a random nearby location, making it a useful, if unpredictable, item for exploration.
questions.question: What unique, teleporting fruit grows on Chorus Trees found throughout the outer End islands?

questions.explanation: The Elytra, a pair of wings that allow the player to glide, is a unique treasure found in an item frame on every End Ship.
questions.question: What unique item, which allows for gliding, can only be found aboard an End Ship?

questions.explanation: End Gateway Portals are small portals that generate after the dragon is defeated, providing access to the outer islands where End Cities are found.
questions.question: After the first Ender Dragon is defeated, what small, star-like portals appear around the main island's edge?

questions.explanation: A Dragon Head can be found at the very front of every End Ship, which can be worn by the player or used as a decorative block.
questions.question: What decorative trophy item is found mounted on the bow of every End Ship?

questions.explanation: The Dragon Egg is a unique, decorative block that appears on the exit portal after the first time the Ender Dragon is defeated.
questions.question: What trophy item is left on top of the exit portal after the Ender Dragon is defeated for the first time?

questions.explanation: An Eye of Ender, crucial for locating and activating the End Portal, is crafted by combining an Ender Pearl with Blaze Powder.
questions.question: What two items must be combined to craft an Eye of Ender?

questions.explanation: Players must locate an underground Stronghold to find the End Portal room and begin their journey to The End.
questions.question: In which Overworld structure is the End Portal always located?

meta.lore_desc: A bleak, desolate dimension composed of floating islands of End Stone. It is the final frontier for many players, home to the Ender Dragon and the mysterious End Cities.

questions.explanation: Cave Spiders are smaller, more dangerous relatives of regular spiders that can poison players. Their spawners are frequently found in mineshafts.
questions.question: What venomous, blue-colored spider variant is commonly found in mineshafts, often from a spawner?

questions.explanation: Mineshafts are characterized by their wooden support structures, using wood planks for floors and fences as pillars and railings.
questions.question: What are the long corridors in a mineshaft primarily constructed from?

questions.explanation: Mineshafts are notoriously filled with cobwebs, which can slow down players and mobs that walk through them.
questions.question: What block is found in abundance throughout mineshafts, often obscuring pathways?

questions.explanation: In addition to regular chests, players can find Minecarts with Chests sitting on the rails, containing valuable loot.
questions.question: What special type of chest can be found within mineshafts?

questions.explanation: Incomplete railway systems are a key feature of mineshafts, hinting at their original purpose.
questions.question: What is laid along the floor of many mineshaft tunnels?

questions.explanation: In the Badlands biome (formerly Mesa), mineshafts can generate on the surface, making them much easier to find and explore.
questions.question: In which biome are mineshafts known to generate at or above the surface level?

questions.explanation: Mineshafts that generate in the Badlands biome are uniquely constructed using Dark Oak planks and fences instead of the usual Oak.
questions.question: What type of wood are the support beams in a Badlands mineshaft made from?

questions.explanation: Mineshaft chests are one of the few places in the game where the incredibly rare and powerful Enchanted Golden Apple can be found.
questions.question: Which of these valuable items has a chance to be found in a mineshaft chest?

questions.explanation: When a mineshaft crosses a chasm, the bridges are either suspended from above by chains or supported from below by log pillars.
questions.question: When mineshafts generate across a ravine or large cave, what supports the wooden pathways?

questions.explanation: Exploring large ravines is a common strategy for finding mineshafts, as the chasms often cut through the tunnel systems, leaving them exposed.
questions.question: What common underground feature often intersects with and exposes sections of a mineshaft?

questions.explanation: Gold ore generates more frequently and at higher elevations in the Badlands biome, and since mineshafts also generate higher up, they become hotspots for finding gold.
questions.question: In Badlands biomes, the higher generation level of mineshafts makes it a particularly good place to find which ore?

questions.explanation: Because mineshafts generate first, ore veins can then generate on top of them, sometimes replacing blocks like wooden planks or rails.
questions.question: Mineshafts generate before other chunk features. What does this mean for ore generation?
wrong: Ores will not spawn near mineshafts

questions.explanation: The tunnels themselves are a 3x3 block space, allowing for easy passage and the placement of rails down the center.
questions.question: What is the internal size of a standard mineshaft corridor, not including the support beams?

questions.explanation: When a mineshaft generation path would intersect with a body of water or lava, a solid barrier is generated to block the fluid, which can sometimes wall off entire sections of the structure.
questions.question: What do mineshafts generate to prevent water or lava from flowing in when they intersect with an aquifer?

meta.lore_desc: A sprawling network of abandoned tunnels and supports found deep underground. These structures are a remnant of a past civilization, filled with cobwebs, rickety rails, and hidden treasures.

questions.explanation: These imposing structures are constructed almost entirely from dark red Nether Bricks and their variants like fences and stairs.
questions.question: What is the primary material that Nether Fortresses are made of?

questions.explanation: Blazes are hostile mobs made of fire and smoke that spawn naturally and from spawners within Nether Fortresses.
questions.question: Which flying, fiery mob that shoots fireballs is found exclusively in Nether Fortresses?

questions.explanation: Blazes are the sole source of Blaze Rods, which are essential for brewing potions and crafting the Eyes of Ender needed to reach The End.
questions.question: Killing a Blaze is the only way to obtain which important crafting item?

questions.explanation: Wither Skeletons are dangerous mobs that spawn only within the boundaries of a Nether Fortress.
questions.question: Which tall, dark skeleton wields a stone sword and can inflict the 'Wither' effect?

questions.explanation: Nether Wart is a vital ingredient for brewing most potions and is primarily found in small gardens within Nether Fortresses.
questions.question: What is the name of the crucial potion ingredient that grows on Soul Sand in Nether Fortresses?

questions.explanation: Nether Fortresses have their own unique mob spawning list which includes Zombified Piglins, Skeletons, and Magma Cubes.
questions.question: Besides Wither Skeletons and Blazes, which of these common mobs can also spawn within a fortress?

questions.explanation: Collecting three Wither Skeleton Skulls allows a player to construct and summon the Wither, a powerful boss.
questions.question: What is the rare head-drop from a Wither Skeleton used for?

questions.explanation: A fortress consists of interior, enclosed corridors and exterior, open-air bridges that connect different sections over the Nether wastes.
questions.question: Structurally, Nether Fortresses are made of two main types of areas: enclosed corridors and what else?

questions.explanation: Chests within a Nether Fortress can contain a variety of valuable loot, including diamonds, gold ingots, saddles, and horse armor.
questions.question: Which of these valuable items can be found in Nether Fortress chests?

questions.explanation: As creatures of fire, Blazes take damage from snowballs, making them a surprisingly effective, though unconventional, weapon against them.
questions.question: Blazes are notably vulnerable to what common throwable item?

questions.explanation: Even though Ghasts are iconic to the Nether, they are not on the fortress's specific spawn list and will not spawn within its boundaries.
questions.question: Nether Fortresses have their own mob spawn list, which overrides the spawns of the Nether biome they are in. What mob notably does NOT spawn inside a fortress?

questions.explanation: Bastion Remnants are large, blackstone structures inhabited by Piglins and Piglin Brutes, and are a separate structure from the Nether Brick fortresses.
questions.question: What is the name of the other large structure made of dark blocks found in the Nether, often confused with a fortress?

questions.explanation: Blaze spawners are unique in that they can spawn Blazes at a light level of 11 or lower, much higher than most hostile mobs.
questions.question: What is the minimum light level at which Blazes can spawn from their spawner?

questions.explanation: When the game decides to spawn a skeleton in a fortress, there is an 80% chance for it to be a Wither Skeleton and a 20% chance for it to be a regular skeleton.
questions.question: What is the probability that a Skeleton spawning inside a Nether Fortress will be a Wither Skeleton?

questions.explanation: Placing Nether Bricks in a stonecutter or furnace allows you to create Chiseled Nether Bricks, which feature a Wither Skeleton's face.
questions.question: What decorative block with a Wither Skeleton skull pattern can be crafted using Nether Bricks?

meta.lore_desc: A massive, dark, and imposing structure found in the Nether. Made of Nether Bricks, these fortresses are a critical location for progression, housing dangerous mobs and essential resources.

questions.explanation: Pikachu is one of the most famous Electric-type Pokémon, capable of learning powerful moves like Thunder Shock and Thunderbolt.
questions.question: What is the primary Pokémon type of Pikachu?

questions.explanation: In Pokémon Yellow, Professor Oak gives you a Pikachu as your starter instead of the usual choice of Bulbasaur, Charmander, or Squirtle.
questions.question: In the 'Pokémon Yellow' version of the game, Pikachu is unique because it's received as what?
wrong: A prize from the Game Corner

questions.explanation: Pikachu's iconic red cheeks are actually electrical sacs that generate and store electricity, which can be discharged in powerful attacks.
questions.question: What prominent physical feature on Pikachu's face is used to store electricity?

questions.explanation: Unlike most Pokémon that evolve by leveling up, Pikachu requires the use of a Thunder Stone to evolve into its more powerful form, Raichu.
questions.question: What is the name of the evolutionary stone required to evolve Pikachu into Raichu?

questions.explanation: When exposed to a Thunder Stone, Pikachu evolves into Raichu, a larger and more powerful Electric-type Pokémon.
questions.question: What is the name of Pikachu's more powerful, evolved form?

questions.explanation: Wild Pikachu have a small chance of appearing in Viridian Forest, making it one of the earliest opportunities for players to catch one.
questions.question: In 'Pokémon Red and Blue', what is one of the two primary locations where you can catch a wild Pikachu?

questions.explanation: Lt. Surge, known as 'The Lightning American', is the Gym Leader of Vermilion City and a master of Electric-types, with his ace Pokémon being a powerful Raichu.
questions.question: Which Vermilion City Gym Leader specializes in Electric-type Pokémon and features a Raichu on their team?

questions.explanation: The abandoned Power Plant is filled with powerful Electric-type Pokémon, including wild Pikachu and their evolved form, Raichu.
questions.question: Besides Viridian Forest, which optional, high-level area in Kanto is also home to wild Pikachu in 'Red and Blue'?

questions.explanation: A unique feature of 'Pokémon Yellow' is the ability to check your starter Pikachu's feelings toward you by turning around and speaking to it.
questions.question: In 'Pokémon Yellow', your starter Pikachu follows you around on the overworld. What does it do if you interact with it?

questions.explanation: Thunder Shock, an early-game Electric move, has a 10% chance of leaving the target paralyzed, potentially preventing them from attacking.
questions.question: The move 'Thunder Shock' is a staple for Pikachu. What status condition does it have a chance of inflicting on the opponent?

questions.explanation: This in-game trade allows players to obtain an Electrode, but it requires them to give up a Raichu, Pikachu's evolved form.
questions.question: In the Cinnabar Island laboratory of 'Red and Blue', a scientist will offer to trade you an Electrode for which Pokémon?

questions.explanation: Before the Physical/Special split in later generations, all Electric-type attacks calculated damage based on the Special stat.
questions.question: In Generation I, all Electric-type moves, such as those used by Pikachu, were classified under which attack category?

questions.explanation: Defeating the Vermilion City Gym Leader rewards the player with TM24, which contains Thunderbolt, a significant upgrade over Thunder Shock for any Electric-type.
questions.question: Which TM, given as a reward for defeating Lt. Surge, can be used to teach Pikachu the powerful move 'Thunderbolt'?

meta.lore_desc: An iconic Electric-type Pokémon known for the red pouches on its cheeks where it stores electricity. It can release powerful jolts of lightning when threatened or excited.

questions.explanation: The Fire-type starter, Charmander, evolves into Charmeleon at level 16, and then into the powerful Charizard at level 36.
questions.question: Charizard is the final evolution of which Kanto starter Pokémon?

questions.explanation: Despite its dragon-like appearance, Charizard is a Fire/Flying-type Pokémon, which grants it immunity to Ground-type moves but gives it a major weakness to Rock-type attacks.
questions.question: In addition to its Fire typing, what is Charizard's secondary type?

questions.explanation: Charizard's iconic status was cemented by its appearance on the cover of 'Pokémon Red', making it one of the most recognizable Pokémon in the franchise.
questions.question: Which Pokémon is featured on the box art for the North American release of 'Pokémon Red'?

questions.explanation: Charmander evolves into Charmeleon, which then evolves into Charizard, completing the three-stage evolutionary line.
questions.question: What is the name of the Pokémon that evolves into Charizard?

questions.explanation: Your rival always picks the starter Pokémon that has a type advantage over yours, so he will have Charizard if you start with the Grass-type Bulbasaur.
questions.question: Your rival, Blue, will have a Charizard on his Champion team if you chose which Pokémon as your starter?

questions.explanation: Flamethrower is a classic and powerful Fire-type attack, a staple move for Pokémon like Charizard, known for its high power and chance to burn.
questions.question: Which powerful Fire-type move, learned via TM, involves the user firing a massive burst of flame that may leave the target with a burn?

questions.explanation: As a Flying-type, Charizard is a natural choice for learning HM02 Fly, allowing for fast travel across the Kanto region.
questions.question: Charizard can learn an HM that allows the player to travel to previously visited towns. What is this move?

questions.explanation: Lance is the final member of the Elite Four and a master of Dragon-types like Dragonite, which shares a similar appearance and power level to Charizard.
questions.question: Which member of the Elite Four specializes in Dragon-type Pokémon, a type that Charizard resembles?

questions.explanation: Fire Spin was a notoriously powerful move in Generation I, trapping the opponent and dealing continuous Fire-type damage, preventing them from switching out or attacking.
questions.question: The move 'Fire Spin' traps the opponent for several turns. What type of damage does it inflict each turn?

questions.explanation: After defeating Blaine, the Fire-type Gym Leader of Cinnabar Island, he awards the player with TM38, which contains the high-power, lower-accuracy move Fire Blast.
questions.question: The TM for the powerful move 'Fire Blast' can be found as a prize from which Gym Leader?

questions.explanation: Surprisingly, Charizard could learn the powerful Ground-type move Earthquake via TM, giving it a powerful and unexpected weapon against Electric-type foes.
questions.question: Which powerful Ground-type move could be taught to Charizard via TM26 to counter its Electric-type weakness?

questions.explanation: TM03, Swords Dance, could be taught to a wide range of Pokémon, including Charizard, to double their Attack stat and sweep through opponents.
questions.question: Which status-raising move could Charizard learn via TM that sharply boosts its Attack stat?

questions.explanation: Prior to Generation IV, all moves of a certain type were either Physical or Special. All Fire-type moves, like Flamethrower, were categorized as Special.
questions.question: In Generation I, all Fire-type moves were classified as which kind of attack?

meta.lore_desc: The final evolution of Charmander. This Fire/Flying-type Pokémon resembles a European dragon. Its fiery breath is hot enough to melt boulders, and it is known for seeking out powerful opponents.

questions.explanation: The Water-type starter, Squirtle, evolves into Wartortle at level 16, and finally into the tank-like Blastoise at level 36.
questions.question: Blastoise is the final form of which starter Pokémon?

questions.explanation: Blastoise is a pure Water-type Pokémon, giving it weaknesses to Grass and Electric types, but resistance to Fire, Water, and Ice.
questions.question: What is the primary Pokémon type of Blastoise?

questions.explanation: Blastoise is famous for the two large water cannons that retract from its shell, capable of shooting water with incredible force.
questions.question: What iconic features on Blastoise's shell are used to fire powerful jets of water?

questions.explanation: Your rival always chooses the starter with a type advantage over yours. If you pick the Fire-type Charmander, he will choose the Water-type Squirtle, which eventually becomes Blastoise.
questions.question: Your rival, Blue, will have a Blastoise on his team if you chose which Pokémon as your starter?

questions.explanation: Squirtle's evolutionary line proceeds from Squirtle to Wartortle, and finally to Blastoise.
questions.question: What is the name of the Pokémon that evolves into Blastoise?

questions.explanation: Misty, known as 'The Tomboyish Mermaid', is the second Gym Leader in Kanto and a master of Water-type Pokémon like Staryu and Starmie.
questions.question: Which Cerulean City Gym Leader specializes in Water-type Pokémon?

questions.explanation: Hydro Pump is one of the strongest Water-type moves, projecting a huge volume of water under immense pressure to strike the foe.
questions.question: What is the name of the powerful Water-type move, often considered Blastoise's signature attack, that fires a massive blast of water?

questions.explanation: HM03 Surf is a powerful Water-type attack in battle and is essential for navigating the Kanto region's waterways, which Blastoise can learn.
questions.question: Blastoise can learn a move via HM that allows the player to travel across bodies of water on the map. What is this move?

questions.explanation: By retreating into its hard shell, Blastoise can use Withdraw to increase its already formidable Defense, making it even harder to take down with physical attacks.
questions.question: Which defensive move, learned naturally by the Squirtle line, raises the user's Defense stat?

questions.explanation: Lorelei is the first member of the Kanto Elite Four and a master of Ice-type Pokémon, which pose a significant threat to Water-types like Blastoise.
questions.question: Which member of the Elite Four specializes in Ice-type Pokémon, one of the two types super-effective against Blastoise?

questions.explanation: For a high price in coins, players could acquire the TM for Hyper Beam, an incredibly powerful attack usable by many fully-evolved Pokémon like Blastoise.
questions.question: What powerful Normal-type move, which requires a turn to recharge after use, could Blastoise learn from a TM purchased at the Celadon Game Corner?

questions.explanation: Teaching Blastoise Ice Beam or Blizzard was a popular strategy, as it provided excellent coverage against the Grass-type Pokémon that would otherwise threaten it.
questions.question: To counter its weakness to Grass-types, which powerful Ice-type move could Blastoise learn via TM13?

questions.explanation: Bite is a Normal-type move in Generation I that Blastoise learns naturally, giving it a quick attack that can sometimes prevent the opponent from moving.
questions.question: What biting move does Blastoise learn by leveling up that has a chance to make the opponent flinch?

questions.explanation: Before the Physical/Special split, all Water-type moves, from Water Gun to Hydro Pump, calculated damage using the Special stat.
questions.question: In Generation I, all Water-type moves were classified under which attack category?

meta.lore_desc: The final evolution of Squirtle. This large, shelled Pokémon is known for the high-pressure water cannons on its back, which are powerful enough to punch through steel.

questions.explanation: The dual Grass/Poison-type starter, Bulbasaur, evolves into Ivysaur at level 16, and then into the mighty Venusaur at level 32.
questions.question: Venusaur is the final evolution of which starter Pokémon?

questions.explanation: The entire Bulbasaur line shares the Grass/Poison typing, giving it key resistances to Fighting and Grass, but also weaknesses to Psychic and Flying.
questions.question: In addition to Grass, what is Venusaur's secondary type?

questions.explanation: Bulbasaur evolves into Ivysaur, which is recognizable by the budding flower on its back, before fully blooming upon evolving into Venusaur.
questions.question: What is the name of the Pokémon that evolves into Venusaur?

questions.explanation: Your rival always picks the starter that is super-effective against yours. Therefore, if you pick the Water-type Squirtle, he will pick the Grass-type Bulbasaur.
questions.question: Your rival will choose Venusaur as his final Pokémon if you started your journey with which Pokémon?

questions.explanation: Bulbasaur is born with a large seed on its back, which sprouts and grows into a bud on Ivysaur, and finally blossoms into a large flower on Venusaur.
questions.question: The plant on Venusaur's back is a fully bloomed version of what was on Bulbasaur's back. What was it?

questions.explanation: Erika, known as 'The Nature-Loving Princess', is the Gym Leader of Celadon City and exclusively uses Grass-type Pokémon like Vileplume and Tangela.
questions.question: Which Celadon City Gym Leader is a master of Grass-type Pokémon?

questions.explanation: Leech Seed is a signature move for many Grass-types, sapping the opponent's health at the end of each turn and restoring the user's.
questions.question: What is the name of the Grass-type move that plants a seed in the opponent to drain their health each turn?

questions.explanation: HM01 Cut allows players to clear certain obstacles on the world map and can be taught to Pokémon like Venusaur.
questions.question: Venusaur can learn an HM move that allows the player to chop down small trees that block paths. What is it?

questions.explanation: Solar Beam is a devastating Grass-type attack where the user gathers light on the first turn and unleashes a powerful beam on the second.
questions.question: What is the most powerful Grass-type move Venusaur learns by leveling up, which requires a turn to charge sunlight before attacking?

questions.explanation: As a Poison-type, Venusaur can use moves like Poison Powder to inflict the poison status, which causes the target to lose health every turn.
questions.question: The move 'Poison Powder' is used to inflict what status condition on an opponent?

questions.explanation: In Generation I, the move Growth raised the user's Special stat by one stage, boosting both Special Attack and Special Defense.
questions.question: What move, learned by Venusaur via level-up, sharply raises the user's Special stat in Generation I?

questions.explanation: Razor Leaf was a particularly powerful move in the original games due to its increased chance of landing a critical hit, which ignored the opponent's defensive boosts.
questions.question: What is the name of the Grass-type move Venusaur learns that has a high critical-hit ratio?

questions.explanation: After defeating the Gym Leader Koga, players receive TM06, Toxic, which inflicts a 'badly poisoned' status where the damage increases each turn.
questions.question: Which TM, given to the player in Fuchsia City, can teach Venusaur a move that badly poisons the opponent?

questions.explanation: Before the major gameplay overhaul in later generations, all Grass-type attacks calculated their damage based on the Special stat.
questions.question: In Generation I, all Grass-type moves were classified under which attack category?

questions.explanation: Take Down is a powerful Normal-type physical attack, but it comes with the drawback of inflicting recoil damage equal to 25% of the damage dealt.
questions.question: Which powerful Normal-type move could be taught to Venusaur via TM09 that would cause the user to receive recoil damage?

meta.lore_desc: The final evolution of Bulbasaur. The large flower on its back absorbs sunlight, converting it into energy. The flower's scent can soothe emotions and becomes stronger after rainy days.

questions.explanation: The Poké Flute's melody is the only thing that can rouse a sleeping Snorlax, causing it to stand up and attack.
questions.question: In Pokémon Red and Blue, what musical instrument is required to wake up the two Snorlax blocking key routes?

questions.explanation: Snorlax's typical day is incredibly simple: it eats until it's full, and then it promptly goes to sleep.
questions.question: This Pokémon's daily routine consists almost entirely of eating and what other activity?

questions.explanation: Snorlax is a pure Normal-type Pokémon, which gives it only one weakness: Fighting-type moves.
questions.question: What is Snorlax's Pokémon type in the original Red and Blue games?

questions.explanation: One Snorlax sleeps on Route 12, south of Lavender Town, and the other is found on Route 16, west of Celadon City.
questions.question: In Kanto, one Snorlax blocks the path near Celadon City, while the other blocks a route south of which spooky town?

questions.explanation: This title is officially used in its Pokédex entries, highlighting its most famous characteristic.
questions.question: Because it's often found slumbering, Snorlax is known as the what Pokémon?

questions.explanation: After rescuing Mr. Fuji from the top of Pokémon Tower, he gives you the Poké Flute as a reward.
questions.question: What is the name of the special item you receive from Mr. Fuji that allows you to wake up Snorlax?

questions.explanation: Rest is one of Snorlax's signature moves, allowing it to fully heal itself at the cost of being asleep and vulnerable for a couple of turns.
questions.question: What is the only move Snorlax knows that allows it to recover all of its health by slumbering for two turns?

questions.explanation: There are only two Snorlax available to catch in the entire game; if they are defeated instead of caught, they will not reappear.
questions.question: How many Snorlax can be found and captured in the wild throughout the entire Kanto region in Pokémon Red and Blue?

questions.explanation: The Snorlax on Route 12 blocks the path from Route 11, preventing access to the southern part of the Kanto region.
questions.question: One of the two sleeping Snorlax in Kanto can be found on Route 12, which connects Lavender Town to which other route?

questions.explanation: This Snorlax prevents trainers from taking the western path out of Celadon City towards Cycling Road.
questions.question: The other Snorlax is found blocking the path on Route 16, which is located to the west of what major Kanto city?

questions.explanation: Body Slam is a strong STAB (Same-Type Attack Bonus) move for Snorlax in the original games, with the added benefit of a 30% paralysis chance.
questions.question: In Generation I, Snorlax learns a powerful Normal-type move at level 35 that has a chance to paralyze the opponent. What is this move?

questions.explanation: Amnesia raises the user's Special stat by two stages, making Snorlax's special attacks and special defense formidable.
questions.question: Which Psychic-type move does Snorlax learn naturally in Generation I, significantly boosting its Special stat?

questions.explanation: This hidden feature makes the Poké Flute a surprisingly useful tool in tough battles, saving you from using consumable items.
questions.question: The Poké Flute, used to wake Snorlax, can also be used in battle to wake up any Pokémon that has been put to sleep by an opponent's move, acting as a reusable version of what item?

questions.explanation: Munchlax was introduced in Generation IV and evolves into Snorlax when it levels up with high friendship.
questions.question: The baby Pokémon that evolves into Snorlax, introduced in a later generation, is known by what name?

questions.explanation: The Silph Scope is necessary to navigate the Pokémon Tower and rescue Mr. Fuji, which is the prerequisite for getting the Poké Flute.
questions.question: Before you can receive the Poké Flute from Mr. Fuji, you must first obtain what key item from the Team Rocket Hideout to identify ghosts in the Pokémon Tower?

meta.lore_desc: A very lazy Pokémon that does nothing but eat and sleep. Its stomach can digest any kind of food, even if it's rotten or moldy. It is known for blocking critical paths in the Kanto region.

questions.explanation: Mewtwo is a pure Psychic-type, making it one of the most powerful types in the original Red and Blue games due to a lack of effective counters.
questions.question: What type of Pokémon is the legendary Mewtwo?

questions.explanation: Mewtwo resides in the deepest part of Cerulean Cave, which only becomes accessible after the player has defeated the Elite Four and the Champion.
questions.question: After becoming the Pokémon League Champion, where in the Kanto region can a trainer find and attempt to capture Mewtwo?

questions.explanation: Journal entries found in the Pokémon Mansion on Cinnabar Island describe how scientists discovered and cloned Mew to create Mewtwo.
questions.question: Mewtwo was created by scientists through genetic manipulation of the DNA of which mythical Pokémon?

questions.explanation: Due to Mewtwo's incredibly low catch rate, most players save their one and only Master Ball for a guaranteed capture.
questions.question: What is the name of the powerful, single-use Poké Ball often saved by trainers specifically to catch Mewtwo without fail?

questions.explanation: This species name highlights its origins as a creature born from scientific experimentation rather than natural processes.
questions.question: According to its Pokédex entry, Mewtwo is known as the what Pokémon?

questions.explanation: The Pokémon Mansion on Cinnabar Island is where players can piece together the backstory of Mewtwo's origins.
questions.question: On which Kanto island can you find the ruined Pokémon Mansion containing the journal entries detailing Mewtwo's creation?

questions.explanation: In Generation I, the 'Special' stat governed both Special Attack and Special Defense, and Mewtwo's was the highest in the game, making it a devastating attacker and a resilient tank.
questions.question: In the original games, Mewtwo has the highest base stat total of any Pokémon, particularly excelling in which stat?

questions.explanation: While the games are more ambiguous, other Pokémon media identify Dr. Fuji as the lead scientist behind Mewtwo's creation, connecting him to the kindly Mr. Fuji from Lavender Town.
questions.question: The scientist credited in some adaptations with leading the project that created Mewtwo is named Dr. who?

questions.explanation: The research notes describe how Mewtwo went on a rampage, destroyed the Cinnabar Lab, and escaped into the wild.
questions.question: In the game's lore, after being created, Mewtwo's immense power proved too much for its creators, leading it to do what to the laboratory?

questions.explanation: Mewtwo comes equipped with Psychic, one of the best attacking moves in the game, making the battle to capture it even more challenging.
questions.question: What powerful Psychic-type move does Mewtwo already know when you encounter it in Cerulean Cave?

questions.explanation: Mewtwo's access to the move Recover makes it incredibly difficult to weaken for capture, as it can repeatedly heal itself during the battle.
questions.question: In Pokémon Red and Blue, which of these moves can Mewtwo learn that allows it to restore its own HP?

questions.explanation: Only trainers who have proven their strength by defeating the Elite Four and the Champion are deemed worthy to enter the cave where this powerful Pokémon resides.
questions.question: The cave where Mewtwo is found was known as the 'Unknown Dungeon' in the original Japanese games. What is a trainer required to do before gaining access to it?

questions.explanation: At Level 70, Mewtwo is the highest-level wild Pokémon that can be encountered in the original games, making it a true final challenge for any trainer.
questions.question: What is the base level of the Mewtwo that you encounter in Cerulean Cave in Pokémon Red and Blue?

questions.explanation: Mewtwo's Pokédex number directly follows Dragonite (#149) and precedes its genetic source, Mew (#151).
questions.question: In the game's code, Mewtwo is Pokémon #150 in the Pokédex, immediately preceding which mythical Pokémon?

questions.explanation: Due to a programming oversight, Ghost-type moves had no effect on Psychic-types in Gen 1, making Bug-type attacks the only viable super-effective strategy against Mewtwo.
questions.question: In Generation I, the Psychic type's only weakness was to Bug-type moves. Which of these is a Bug-type move that could be taught to a Pokémon to counter Mewtwo?

meta.lore_desc: A Pokémon created by gene-splicing and DNA engineering. Its cold, glowing eyes strike fear into its enemies. It is said to have the most savage heart among all Pokémon.

questions.explanation: Professor Oak's famous lab, where new trainers begin their journey, is a landmark in the quiet, humble Pallet Town.
questions.question: In which town is Professor Oak's research laboratory located?

questions.explanation: In Pokémon Red and Blue, the choices are Bulbasaur, Charmander, and Squirtle. Pikachu is the starter Pokémon given in Pokémon Yellow.
questions.question: Professor Oak gives the player one of three Pokémon to start their journey. Which of these is NOT one of the choices?

questions.explanation: In the games, your rival is named Blue (though you can name him). In the anime, his counterpart is famously named Gary.
questions.question: What is the name of Professor Oak's grandson, who also serves as the player's main rival?

questions.explanation: Professor Oak's dream is to have a complete record of every Pokémon, a task he gives to promising new trainers by providing them with a Pokédex.
questions.question: What important device does Professor Oak entrust to the player with the goal of creating a complete encyclopedia of all Pokémon?

questions.explanation: He is known worldwide as a Pokémon researcher, studying the habits and characteristics of countless species.
questions.question: Professor Oak is a leading authority in the field of Pokémon what?

questions.explanation: At the start of the game, the player must go to the Viridian City Poké Mart to pick up Oak's Parcel and deliver it back to him in Pallet Town.
questions.question: Professor Oak asks you to deliver a parcel to him from the Poké Mart in which city?

questions.explanation: After you and your rival receive your Pokédexes, Professor Oak gives you both a set of Poké Balls to begin catching Pokémon.
questions.question: What does the player receive from Professor Oak upon returning the custom Poké Ball parcel from Viridian City?

questions.explanation: An aide in the gate on Route 11 will give you the Itemfinder, but only if you have caught at least 30 different kinds of Pokémon.
questions.question: Professor Oak has several aides who work in his lab and appear across the Kanto region. What item does one of his aides give you if you've caught enough Pokémon?

questions.explanation: Your rival will always select the Pokémon that is super-effective against yours: Squirtle beats Charmander, Charmander beats Bulbasaur, and Bulbasaur beats Squirtle.
questions.question: The player's rival always chooses the starter Pokémon that has a type advantage over the one the player picks. If the player chooses Charmander, what will the rival choose?

questions.explanation: Daisy Oak can be found in Pallet Town and will offer to groom one of your Pokémon for free, which increases its friendship.
questions.question: Besides his grandson, Professor Oak also has a granddaughter. What is her name?

questions.explanation: The dummied-out data reveals a very powerful team for Professor Oak, including a Level 66 Tauros, a Level 67 Exeggutor, a Level 68 Arcanine, a Level 70 Gyarados, and the final evolution of the starter Pokémon the player didn't choose.
questions.question: In the game data for Pokémon Red and Blue, a battle against Professor Oak was programmed but ultimately unused. What was the highest-level Pokémon on his team?

questions.explanation: In some Pokémon media, Blaine is not just a Gym Leader but also a respected scientist who has a professional relationship with Professor Oak.
questions.question: Which other famous Pokémon researcher, known for his work on Cinnabar Island, is depicted as a friend and colleague of Professor Oak?

questions.explanation: The Exp. All distributes experience points among all Pokémon in the player's party, even those that did not participate in battle, making it a valuable tool for training.
questions.question: In a gatehouse on Route 15, one of Professor Oak's aides will give you an item if you have caught 50 or more Pokémon. What is this helpful item?

meta.lore_desc: A renowned Pokémon Professor from Pallet Town. He is a leading authority in the field of Pokémon research and gives new trainers their first Pokémon and a Pokédex to begin their journey.

questions.explanation: Brock presides over the Pewter Gym, the first gym a trainer must challenge to enter the Pokémon League in Kanto.
questions.question: Brock is the official Pokémon Gym Leader of which Kanto city?

questions.explanation: Victorious trainers receive the Boulder Badge, the first of the eight badges required to challenge the Kanto Pokémon League.
questions.question: What is the name of the badge awarded to trainers who defeat Brock in a gym battle?

questions.explanation: As the 'rock-solid Pokémon trainer,' Brock exclusively uses Rock-type Pokémon in his gym battles in Red and Blue.
questions.question: Brock specializes in training Pokémon of which elemental type?

questions.explanation: Brock's signature Pokémon and final challenge in the Pewter Gym is his formidable Onix.
questions.question: In Pokémon Red and Blue, Brock's team consists of a Geodude and which other large, serpentine Rock/Ground Pokémon?

questions.explanation: Both Bulbasaur (Grass) and Squirtle (Water) have moves that are super-effective against Brock's Rock/Ground Pokémon, making the battle much easier.
questions.question: Choosing which starter Pokémon at the beginning of the game gives a trainer a significant advantage against Brock's Rock-type team?

questions.explanation: In the original games, Brock's ace Pokémon, Onix, is at level 14, making it a tough early-game opponent.
questions.question: What is the level of Brock's highest-level Pokémon, Onix, in Pokémon Red and Blue?

questions.explanation: Brock rewards trainers with TM34, which teaches the move Bide, where a Pokémon endures attacks for two turns and then returns double the damage.
questions.question: In addition to the Boulder Badge, what TM does Brock give to the player upon defeat in Pokémon Red and Blue?

questions.explanation: Pewter City is famous for its large museum, which features exhibits on space and fossils.
questions.question: The Pewter City Gym is located near what major cultural institution in the city?

questions.explanation: Both Geodude and Onix share the Rock/Ground typing, giving them a 4x weakness to both Grass and Water-type attacks.
questions.question: Rock-type Pokémon like Brock's are doubly weak to which two types, making starters like Bulbasaur and Squirtle so effective?

questions.explanation: While he initially aims to be a great Pokémon Breeder, his dream eventually evolves into wanting to become a Pokémon Doctor to help heal Pokémon.
questions.question: In the Pokémon anime, what is Brock's ultimate career goal, which inspires him to travel with Ash?
wrong: To be the best Rock-type trainer

questions.explanation: A key part of Brock's backstory in the anime is that he was left to care for his nine younger siblings after his parents left.
questions.question: In the anime, Brock has a large family and must care for his many younger what?

questions.explanation: In the anime, Brock's father, Flint, was the original Pewter City Gym Leader before abandoning his post and family.
questions.question: What is the name of Brock's father, who leaves the family to pursue his own Pokémon journey?

questions.explanation: During the Johto saga, Brock's brother Forrest helps his Onix evolve into the powerful Steelix.
questions.question: Brock's Onix eventually evolves into which Steel/Ground type Pokémon in later series of the anime?

questions.explanation: In the Generation II games, Brock can be found training near the Pewter City entrance of Diglett's Cave on certain days of the week.
questions.question: In Pokémon Gold, Silver, and their remakes, where can the player find Brock for a rematch after he has left his gym?

meta.lore_desc: The Gym Leader of Pewter City's Pokémon Gym. A rock-solid trainer with a serious demeanor, he is the first major challenge for trainers starting their journey in the Kanto region.

questions.explanation: Misty is introduced with the title 'The Tomboyish Mermaid' in the original games, reflecting her specialty in Water-type Pokémon and her strong personality.
questions.question: What is Misty's official title as the Gym Leader of Cerulean City?

questions.explanation: Misty is the Gym Leader of Cerulean City, a seaside town in the Kanto region known for its waterways.
questions.question: Which city is home to Misty's Pokémon Gym?

questions.explanation: Misty's Starmie is her strongest Pokémon in the Red and Blue Gym battle, known for its high speed and powerful attacks.
questions.question: Which of these Pokémon is famously Misty's signature powerhouse in her Gym battle?

questions.explanation: As the leader of the Cerulean Gym, Misty is a master of Water-type Pokémon, a fact reflected in her team and the gym's aquatic design.
questions.question: Misty specializes in Pokémon of which elemental type?

questions.explanation: Victorious trainers earn the Cascade Badge from Misty, which allows them to command Pokémon up to level 30.
questions.question: What is the name of the badge awarded to trainers who defeat Misty?

questions.explanation: In Pokémon Red and Blue, Misty's team consists of two Pokémon: a Staryu and its more powerful evolution, Starmie.
questions.question: Besides her signature Starmie, Misty uses which other Pokémon in her Gym battle?

questions.explanation: Upon defeat, Misty awards trainers with TM11, which teaches the move BubbleBeam.
questions.question: The TM that Misty gives out as a reward contains which Water-type move?

questions.explanation: Misty's gym features a large swimming pool with platforms, and trainers must battle her junior swimmers before they can challenge her.
questions.question: The Cerulean Gym, where Misty presides, is filled with what feature that trainers must navigate?

questions.explanation: In Japan, Misty is known as Kasumi, which can mean 'mist,' fitting her theme as a Water-type Gym Leader.
questions.question: In the original Japanese versions, what is Misty's name?

questions.explanation: Misty's Starmie is level 21 in the original Red and Blue games, making it a significant early-game challenge for many trainers.
questions.question: In Pokémon Red and Blue, what level is Misty's powerful Starmie?

questions.explanation: Misty hands over TM11, which teaches BubbleBeam, a reliable Water-type move in Generation I.
questions.question: What is the technical machine number for the BubbleBeam TM that Misty awards?

questions.explanation: It is a popular and well-supported fan theory that Lorelei was the Cerulean Gym Leader before being promoted to the Elite Four, passing the title to her admirer, Misty.
questions.question: In a piece of fan-supported lore, it's suggested that Misty took over the Cerulean Gym from which future Elite Four member?

meta.lore_desc: Known as 'The Tomboyish Mermaid,' Misty is the formidable Gym Leader of Cerulean City. A specialist in Water-type Pokémon, she awards the Cascade Badge to trainers who can overcome her aquatic assault.

questions.explanation: Giovanni is the head of Team Rocket and also secretly serves as the Gym Leader of Viridian City.
questions.question: What is the name of Team Rocket's enigmatic and powerful leader?

questions.explanation: Team Rocket's logo is a large, stylized red 'R', which appears on their uniforms and in their hideouts.
questions.question: What is the signature letter that serves as this criminal organization's logo?

questions.explanation: The Rocket Game Corner in Celadon City serves as a front for their secret underground base.
questions.question: In Celadon City, Team Rocket operates a secret hideout underneath which establishment?

questions.explanation: Throughout Kanto, the common Team Rocket Grunts are frequently seen battling with Rattata, Zubat, and their evolutions.
questions.question: Which two Pokémon are most commonly used by low-level Team Rocket Grunts?

questions.explanation: Team Rocket aims to take over the world by stealing and exploiting powerful Pokémon for their own nefarious purposes.
questions.question: Team Rocket's ultimate goal is to use Pokémon to achieve what?

questions.explanation: Team Rocket launches a full-scale takeover of the Silph Co. headquarters in an attempt to steal the Master Ball prototype.
questions.question: What major Kanto corporation's headquarters in Saffron City does Team Rocket take over?

questions.explanation: After defeating Giovanni in the Celadon City hideout, he leaves behind the Silph Scope, a device needed to identify the ghosts in the Pokémon Tower.
questions.question: To reveal the ghosts in Lavender Town's Pokémon Tower, players must retrieve what item from Giovanni in the Rocket Hideout?

questions.explanation: A Team Rocket Grunt guards a poster on the back wall; after defeating him, the player can press a hidden switch behind it to reveal the stairs.
questions.question: The secret switch to enter the Rocket Hideout is hidden behind what object in the Game Corner?

questions.explanation: The player first encounters Team Rocket in Mt. Moon, where they are trying to steal rare Pokémon fossils to resurrect and sell.
questions.question: In Mt. Moon, what are the Team Rocket Grunts attempting to steal and sell?

questions.explanation: In his final battle as a Gym Leader, Giovanni's most powerful Pokémon is a high-level Rhydon.
questions.question: What is the final Pokémon Giovanni uses in his Viridian City Gym battle?

questions.explanation: As the final Gym Leader, Giovanni bestows the Earth Badge upon trainers who can defeat his team of Ground-type Pokémon.
questions.question: Before Giovanni takes over, the Viridian City Gym is initially closed. What badge does he eventually award?

questions.explanation: A grateful Silph Co. employee entrusts the player with a Lapras to prevent it from falling into Team Rocket's hands.
questions.question: During the Silph Co. takeover, a scientist on the 5th floor gives the player what rare Pokémon to keep it safe from Team Rocket?

questions.explanation: To reach Giovanni in the lowest level of the hideout, the player must first find the Lift Key, which is dropped by a grunt on the B4F.
questions.question: What is the name of the key item needed to operate the elevator inside the Rocket Hideout?

questions.explanation: The ghost blocking the way in Pokémon Tower is the spirit of a Marowak that was killed by Team Rocket, leaving its child Cubone an orphan.
questions.question: In Pokémon Tower, Team Rocket's actions led to the unrestful spirit of which Pokémon haunting the upper floors?

meta.lore_desc: A villainous organization aiming for world domination through the exploitation of Pokémon. Led by the mysterious Giovanni, their schemes range from stealing fossils to taking over major corporations, always recognizable by their signature 'R' logo.

questions.explanation: The Poké Ball is the fundamental item used by trainers to capture wild Pokémon and carry them on their adventures.
questions.question: What is the primary function of a Poké Ball?

questions.explanation: The classic Poké Ball design features a red top half, a white bottom half, and a black band with a white button in the center.
questions.question: What are the iconic colors of a standard Poké Ball?

questions.explanation: The Master Ball is the most powerful Poké Ball ever created, capable of catching any Pokémon without fail.
questions.question: Which type of Poké Ball has a perfect, 100% success rate and can never fail to catch a Pokémon?

questions.explanation: Silph Co., based in Saffron City, is the leading manufacturer of trainer supplies in Kanto, including all types of Poké Balls.
questions.question: In Pokémon Red and Blue, which company is the primary manufacturer of Poké Balls?

questions.explanation: The Great Ball is the first upgraded Poké Ball that trainers can purchase, offering a 1.5x catch rate modifier compared to the standard version.
questions.question: A blue and red Poké Ball that has a higher success rate than a standard one is known as what?

questions.explanation: The Ultra Ball is the best commercially available Poké Ball in the Kanto region, providing a 2x catch rate modifier.
questions.question: Which high-performance Poké Ball, featuring a black and yellow design, is even more effective than a Great Ball?

questions.explanation: After liberating Silph Co. from Team Rocket, the company's president rewards the player with the prototype Master Ball.
questions.question: The one-of-a-kind Master Ball is given to the player by the president of which company as a reward?

questions.explanation: The Safari Ball is a special type of Poké Ball that can only be used within the Safari Zone to catch the unique Pokémon found there.
questions.question: A special Poké Ball with a camouflage pattern, used exclusively in a specific area of Fuchsia City, is called what?

questions.explanation: Upon paying the entry fee for the Safari Game, the player receives 30 Safari Balls to use for the duration of their visit.
questions.question: When entering the Safari Zone, how many Safari Balls is the player given to use?

questions.explanation: A standard Poké Ball can be purchased from any Poké Mart for 200 Poké Dollars.
questions.question: What is the standard price of a single Poké Ball at any Poké Mart in the Kanto region?

questions.explanation: The more effective Great Ball costs three times as much as a standard Poké Ball, priced at 600 Poké Dollars.
questions.question: What is the price of a Great Ball at a Poké Mart?

questions.explanation: The high-performance Ultra Ball is the most expensive one available for regular purchase, costing 1200 Poké Dollars.
questions.question: What is the price of an Ultra Ball at a Poké Mart?

questions.explanation: Due to a programming oversight in Generation I, the Safari Ball has the exact same catch rate modifier as an Ultra Ball.
questions.question: In the game's code, the Safari Ball is functionally identical to which other type of Poké Ball?

questions.correct: In a clearing in the northwest
questions.explanation: A Poké Ball can be found as a collectible item on the ground in a small clearing in the northwest section of Viridian Forest.
questions.question: Besides buying them, where can a player find a free Poké Ball item on the ground in Viridian Forest?
wrong: Behind a Cut-able tree near the exit

questions.explanation: In the Safari Zone, traditional Pokémon battles are forbidden. Instead, trainers must use Bait to make Pokémon less likely to flee, or Rocks to make them easier to catch, before throwing a Safari Ball.
questions.question: Which of these is NOT an option when a player encounters a wild Pokémon in the Safari Zone?

meta.lore_desc: The quintessential tool for any Pokémon Trainer. This iconic red-and-white sphere is a technological marvel used to capture wild Pokémon and carry them on their journey. Stronger variants exist for tougher catches.

questions.explanation: Professor Oak, the leading Pokémon researcher in the Kanto region, entrusts the player and their rival with a Pokédex to help with his research.
questions.question: Which famous Pokémon Professor gives the player their Pokédex at the start of their journey?

questions.explanation: The Pokédex is an electronic encyclopedia that automatically records information about any Pokémon the trainer has seen or captured.
questions.question: What is the primary function of the Pokédex?

questions.explanation: The original Kanto Pokédex lists 150 Pokémon. The 151st, Mew, is a mythical Pokémon not required for completion.
questions.question: Professor Oak's dream is for the player to complete the Pokédex by catching how many original Pokémon?

questions.explanation: Professor Oak's lab, where the journey begins, is located in the player's hometown of Pallet Town.
questions.question: Where does Professor Oak have his research laboratory?

questions.explanation: Blue (often referred to as Gary in the anime) is Professor Oak's grandson and the player's competitive rival throughout the game.
questions.question: What is the name of Professor Oak's grandson, who is also the player's main rival?

questions.explanation: The Poké Mart clerk in Viridian City gives the player 'Oak's Parcel,' which they must take back to the professor to receive the Pokédex for themselves and their rival.
questions.question: What item must the player deliver to Professor Oak from the Viridian City Poké Mart to receive their Pokédex?

questions.explanation: The Kanto Pokédex begins with the Grass-type starter, Bulbasaur, as Pokémon #001.
questions.question: Which Pokémon is listed as #001 in the Kanto Pokédex?

questions.explanation: As a token of recognition for completing the monumental task, Professor Oak congratulates the player and they receive a diploma that can be viewed in their house.
questions.question: What reward does Professor Oak give the player for showing him a completed Pokédex?

questions.explanation: The Pokédex allows the player to listen to the unique cry of any Pokémon they have successfully caught.
questions.question: In addition to a picture and description, what sound-based feature does the Pokédex offer for each captured Pokémon?

questions.explanation: By selecting the 'Area' function on a Pokémon's entry, the Pokédex will display on the world map the routes and locations where that species is known to live.
questions.question: The Pokédex has a function that allows the player to view the locations where a captured Pokémon can be found. What is this feature called?

questions.explanation: The original Base Set of the Pokémon Trading Card Game in Japan identifies the Pokédex as model HANDY505 in its card text.
questions.question: In the Japanese Trading Card Game, one model of the Kanto Pokédex is identified by what model number?

questions.explanation: Though rarely used in the games, Professor Oak's full name is revealed in other media to be Samuel Oak.
questions.question: What is Professor Oak's first name?

questions.explanation: One of Professor Oak's aides can be found in the gatehouse on Route 15. If the player has caught 50 or more Pokémon, he will give them the Exp. All, an item that shares experience points among the entire party.
questions.question: In the original Red and Blue games, what does Professor Oak's aide, located on Route 15, give the player for having caught 50 or more species of Pokémon?

meta.lore_desc: An indispensable, high-tech encyclopedia for Pokémon Trainers. This device, given by Professor Oak, records data on any Pokémon that are seen or captured, with the ultimate goal of completing a comprehensive list of all known species.

questions.explanation: Professor Oak is a famed Pokémon researcher who gives new trainers from Pallet Town their first Pokémon and a Pokédex.
questions.question: Who is the esteemed Pokémon Professor residing in Pallet Town who entrusts you with your very first Pokémon?

questions.explanation: Bulbasaur, the Seed Pokémon, is the Grass/Poison-type starter given out by Professor Oak. It is known for being a good choice for beginners.
questions.question: Which of the three starter Pokémon available in Pallet Town is a Grass/Poison type?

questions.explanation: Blue is Professor Oak's grandson and your main rival. He always picks the Pokémon that has a type advantage over yours.
questions.question: What is the name of your lifelong rival who also begins his Pokémon journey in Pallet Town?

questions.explanation: The player's journey begins in their own room, in their house in Pallet Town, where their Mom wishes them well on their adventure.
questions.question: From which building in Pallet Town do you begin your adventure?

questions.explanation: After you deliver a parcel to Professor Oak, he gives both you and your rival a Pokédex, an electronic encyclopedia of Pokémon.
questions.question: What important item for tracking Pokémon does Professor Oak give you before you leave town?

questions.explanation: The clerk at the Viridian City Poké Mart asks you to deliver Oak's Parcel to the professor. Inside is a custom Poké Ball he ordered.
questions.question: What item must you deliver to Professor Oak from the Viridian City Poké Mart before he gives you a Pokédex?

questions.explanation: While your Mom also gives you one, Daisy Oak will give you a Town Map if you speak to her after getting your Pokédex.
questions.question: What does your rival's sister, Daisy Oak, give to you as a gift in her house?

questions.explanation: Your rival always chooses the starter Pokémon that has a type advantage over yours. Water-type Squirtle is strong against Fire-type Charmander.
questions.question: If you choose Charmander as your starter, which Pokémon will your rival choose?

questions.explanation: When surfing or fishing with any rod in Pallet Town, the only Pokémon you can encounter is the Water/Poison-type, Tentacool.
questions.question: What is the only type of wild Pokémon that can be encountered by fishing in Pallet Town's waters?

questions.explanation: As you try to leave Pallet Town for the first time, Professor Oak calls out to you, warning you of the danger of wild Pokémon and leading you back to his lab.
questions.question: What does Professor Oak do to prevent you from walking into the tall grass on Route 1 without a Pokémon?

questions.explanation: The sign at the entrance of Pallet Town reads: "Pallet Town - A Pure White Beginning."
questions.question: What is the town's official slogan, often seen on a sign at the entrance?

questions.explanation: Pallet Town is very small, consisting of only three buildings: the player's house, the rival's house, and Professor Oak's Laboratory.
questions.question: Besides your house and your rival's house, what is the only other building in Pallet Town?

questions.explanation: In the original Japanese releases, Pallet Town was named マサラタウン (Masara Town).
questions.question: In the Japanese versions of the games, Pallet Town is known by what name?

questions.explanation: Before you even get a Pokémon, you can withdraw a single Potion from your PC, which can come in handy for your first battle against your rival.
questions.question: What item can be found by checking the PC in your character's bedroom at the start of the game?

questions.explanation: Route 21 is the sea route that connects Pallet Town to Cinnabar Island, though you'll need a Pokémon that knows Surf to traverse it.
